artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal preferred drawing from life, often sketching outdoors with the subject being nature studies, landscapes, figure drawings and animals. In this first sketch of a series of six sketches of monkeys in the album, Nandalal studies the the head of a monkey in two different templates. He renders the sketch in quick short strokes and slight shading that define the contours of the forms and bring out the underlying expression of mischief.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal was revolutionary in asserting the importance of drawing to the artist's practice of grasping the essence and creative rhythm of the subject. In this sketch. he depicts a goat, rendered in fine, short strokes. He has also studied the head of the goat in a smaller template by the side. As per the inscription, the drawing has been sketched at Patisar, a village in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that reads "Patisar", written twice, along the left and the lower margins. There is another inscription in Bengali that reads "Rajpatra", along the lower margin.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch Nandalal studies the head of a goat in profile, quickly executed in strong, brisk strokes. As per the inscription, the drawing has been sketched at Patisar, a village in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered. As Dinkar Kowshik in his article 'Drawings and Sketches of Nandalal' in the book, 'Nandalal Bose- A Collection of Essays' elucidates, "Much of his (Nandalal's) strength and sensitive wealth finds expression in the spontaneity of his sketches."

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along with the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Patisar", along the left margin.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch Nandalal renders a line drawing of a deer, quickly executed in swift, long strokes, sparing much detail. In his book 'On Art' the artist mentions, "To acquire right knowledge and perception one should study men and animals when they are on the move or are active: when one can note in action the how and wherefore of the body's muscles, tendons and joints."

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: This sketch depicts a horse grazing in a field, reproduced in fine, confident outlines defining the structure of its muscular body. With swift, calligraphic strokes, Nandalal represents the horse's characteristic features and conveys its mood. The slight shading depicts the play of light and shade over the animal.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch, Nandalal portrays two galloping horses, with riders, executed quickly in firm outlines. The long, stiff strokes, delineated in an illustrative manner, convey the hurried movement of the horses, lending energy and life to the sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal was revolutionary in asserting the importance of drawing to the artist's practice of grasping the essence and creative rhythm of the subject. In this first sketch of a series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts a small herd of buffaloes along with their young herders. He carefully brings out the nuances of the animal's body with strong outlines, swift strokes and light shading. The smudged strokes depict the playful herders.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '29 October'1917' in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Khargpur" below the date.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the second in the series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts a buffalo herder giving a bath to his buffalo. He renders the quick sketch in bold, wiry outlines delineated in an illustrative manner.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '3 November'1917' in the bottom-left corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali, roughly translated as 'the tree' in English.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this third sketch of a series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts an Ox, ridden by a young boy. With confident, bold outlines and calligraphic strokes that define the structure of its body, Nandalal conveys the loping movement and characteristic features of the animal. He depicts the young rider in a simple line drawing.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali, twice, along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the fourth in a series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts a bull, grazing in the field. He renders the animal in strong, stiff outlines, delineated in an illustrative manner. The sharp strokes and light shading add depth and volume to the sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Paruldanga". There is also an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Sukumar Dey. Italy tour."

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the fifth in a series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts a cow, carefully rendered in deep, dark outlines, defining its characteristic features. Swift, short strokes have been used to depict the folds of its skin, lending depth to the form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal has in this monochromatic painting, emphasised the tonal variations for precise and recognisable variations. In this sixth sketch of a series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts a calf and a fawn. He carefully renders the subjects in light, confident strokes of watercolour, enhancing its translucent quality and lending texture to the depiction.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of seven sketches of cattle in the album, Nandalal depicts a herd of cows guided by two herders in the fields near Gangtok in Sikkim. He renders the subject in fine, fluid outlines, delineated in an illustrative manner, sparing much detail. The light shading and swift, calligraphic strokes employed by Nandalal lend vigour and life to the entire sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '31 October'1917' along the lower margin of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Gangtok", below the date.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: The fervent sketching of his surroundings, allowed Nandalal to meditate upon the elements of nature. In this first sketch of a series of three sketches of bats in the album, Nandalal depicts a simple line drawing of a flying bat rendered from behind. It is a quick study demarcated with firm outlines, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali, along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of three sketches of bats in the album, Nandalal depicts a flying bat as it spreads its wings. He renders the sketch in sharp, wiry outlines, defining the structure of the form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the second in the series of six sketches of monkeys in the album, Nandalal depicts an anatomical line drawing of a monkey. The quick sketch, rendered in long, loose strokes captures the animal's characteristic expression.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this third sketch of a series of six sketches of monkeys in the album, Nandalal studies a monkey in motion, rendered in a cluster of short, swift strokes. He precisely studies the head of the animal in two different templates rendered in dark outlines and stiff strokes that depict its hairy body. Nandalal also sketches the ear of the monkey in another template.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' and inscribed "Amar Kutir", in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this fourth sketch of a series of six sketches of monkeys in the album, Nandalal studies the head of a monkey in profile. The fine calligraphic strokes and slight shading bring out the underlying anger visible in its expression. He also studies the eyes and hand of the monkey in different templates rendered in swift, short strokes, adding life to the form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal's small sketches are testimony of his keen observation and empathy for the environment in which he lived. In this second sketch of a series of three sketches of bats in the album, Nandalal depicts a simple line drawing of two bats. He renders the mammal in wiry outlines and loose strokes, defining the contours of its form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of six sketches of monkeys in the album, Nandalal studies the head of a monkey in profile. The bold calligraphic strokes bring out the underlying emotion of anger in its expression. Nandalal also studies the head of a monkey from different views depicted in smaller templates on the side.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-left corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this fifth sketch of a series of six sketches of monkeys in the album, Nandalal depicts a monkey sitting on the ground, sketched in profile. The fluid outlines define the contours of the figure and long, loose strokes depict its hairy body. Nandalal also studies the head of a monkey in a smaller template on the side.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal had a firm belief that for the creation of art an intimate understanding of nature and its ways is imperative. In this first sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal reproduces a line drawing of a pigeon. The subject, executed quickly in wiry outlines and long, sharp strokes, is essentially a study in form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this second sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal reproduces three different types of birds, some rendered in fine lines with light shading while others executed quickly in simple line drawings. He also depicts the birds flying or pecking, in small rough templates, rendered in long, loose strokes, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali, twice, along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this third sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal depicts a bird, executed lightly in fluid outlines, defining the structure of its slender body. In a template sketch by the side, Nandalal also depicts a boar rendered in stiff outlines, delineated in an illustrative manner, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: Nandalal small sketches vastly vary in detailing, some drawn quickly with just a few lines, other executed with more elaborate characteristics from an analytical perspective. In this drawing, he portrays a lizard and a chameleon carefully rendered in fluid outlines, defining the contours of their petite forms. The fine detailing and translucency of the colour lend vitality to the sketch. There is also a small template sketch of a scorpion in the bottom-left corner.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali, twice, along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this first sketch of a series of three sketches of ducks in the album, Nandalal depicts a line drawing of a duck's beak. He renders the rough sketch in bold strokes that are strong and quick in character.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali, twice, along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this fourth sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal depicts the bird, Rufous Treepie, commonly known as hanri-chancha in Bengali. The name is derived from the sound made by the bird, which is likened to the sound of scraping the bottom of an earthen pot. In Bengali, hanri means earthen pot and chancha mimics the scraping sound. Nandalal reproduces the bird in quick dabs of watercolour that depict the contours of the fragile form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this second sketch of a series of threes sketches of ducks in the album, Nandalal reproduces the head of a duck in three different templates. With strong, fluid outlines and swift, curvilinear strokes that define the robust form, he depicts its characteristic features. Nandalal also studies the eye of the duck in a smaller template, executed in dark bold outlines.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this fifth sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal depicts a flock of Rufous Treepie bird, on the banks of a water body. He renders the subject in swift brushstrokes, without outlines. The dabs and dashes of watercolour bring out the form of the birds, adding rhythm and life to the entire sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of three sketches of ducks in the album, Nandalal reproduces a simple line drawing of a duck, sketched in swift outlines. The confident, short strokes lend rhythm and life to the robust form. Nandalal also studies the head of the duck in two different templates, depicting its characteristic features.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has here rendered a quick sketch of a crane, precisely studying its body structure, head and beak in smaller templates. He has also rendered a feather of the plumage, comparing it to the leaves of the flower, 'Golanchapa', as the inscription suggests. The drawing has been reproduced in smooth, flowing strokes, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali, along the right margin of the sketch. There is also an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Golanchapa".

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this sixth sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal depicts two birds of the same type. He has rendered the forms in scribbles, without outlines, in a swift, loose manner.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched the figure of a duck, rendered in fine outlines, closely studying the features of its head and beak. The detailing of the plumage gives a sense of the body in the otherwise sparse depiction.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'N.L.Bose' and dated '2nd August 1920', in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has here rendered a quick sketch of a crane, studying its slender body. The artist reproduces the subject in swift, loose strokes, adding rhythm to the graceful form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of seven sketches of birds in the album, Nandalal has executed a rough drawing of a bird. He renders the subject in swift, loose strokes that define the contours of the form. The artist has also depicted the head of a different bird in a smaller template on the side.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a rabbit in profile, rendered in stark outlines. The dark shading behind the animal depicting its shadow, lends a three dimensional effect to the simple sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali twice, in the bottom-right corner and along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In the sketch above, Nandalal depicts a rabbit in profile, rendered in dark curvilinear strokes. He has also studied the head of the animal as a simple line drawing, in a template sketch on the side.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has here rendered a rough sketch of two deer feeding on the leaves of a plant, in sharp, wiry outlines, defining the contours of their slender bodies. The quick, short strokes of the pencil lend life and vitality to the organic forms.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali at the bottom-left corner of the drawing with pencil.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In the sketch above, Nandalal depicts a bull in profile, depicted in fluid lines, defining the frame of its muscular body. He renders the animal with only a few lyrical strokes, that convey its loping movement and characteristic expression.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: The subject of this second sketch in a series of five sketches of boars in the album, is similar to the first, except more roughly reproduced. Nandalal depicts a similar template of the wild animal lying on the ground, rendered in swift strokes that are blunt and coarse.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the first in a series of five sketches of boars in the album, Nandalal depicts a boar sleeping outside its small dwelling. He renders the hut in the backdrop in a simple line drawing, defining its structure with light, smudged strokes. The animal is briskly sketched using dark, sharp lines of the pencil in contrast to its surroundings.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this third sketch in a series of five sketches of boars in the album, Nandalal depicts a boar in profile, sketched in short stiff strokes, defining the contours of its body. He precisely renders the animal with its characteristic features. Nandalal also depicts a line drawing of a figure in the background and a small template of the boar.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this fourth sketch of a series of five sketches of boars in the album, Nandalal depicts a group of boars roaming among people. He renders the forms lightly in fine lines, defining the contours of their bodies, delineated in an illustrative manner. The subject is approached in a minimalistic style, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '4th November 1917' in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali and English that roughly translates to "Way to Gangtok".

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of five sketches of boars in the album, Nandalal depicts a boar, a sow and a bird. He precisely renders the animals in swift and confident strokes that convey their movements and characteristic expression. Nandalal sketches the bird in lyrical outlines, evoking vitality in the delicate form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Kharagpur", along the signature.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this first sketch of a series of three sketches of dogs in the album, Nandalal depicts a dog in its various postures, studying its head and body in different templates. He renders the subject in light monochrome colour with bold, loose strokes, defining the contours of its body. The translucent quality of the watercolour accentuates the swift strokes employed by Nandalal.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-left corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this second sketch of a series of three sketches of bears in the album, Nandalal depicts a bear in profile, rendered in long, calligraphic strokes, defining the structure of its form. He also studies the form of its head in a smaller template on the side. The loose strokes delineated in the manner of an illustration give a rough effect to the sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this first sketch of a series of three sketches of bears in the album, Nandalal closely studies the head of a bear in profile and three-quarter profile in two different templates. He renders the subject in short, swift strokes, defining the structure of its head. Nandalal in his sketches, explored the various living forms present in nature, studying their characteristic features and movements.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this last sketch of a series of three sketches of bears in the album, Nandalal depicts the head of a bear, closely studying its characteristic facial features. He also studies the eye and feet in smaller templates on the side. Nandalal renders the subject in bold outlines and a cluster of light and dark strokes that define the form of the bear.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal fervently sketched the environs of Santiniketan in Bengal and keenly recorded aspects of rural life from the region. In this first sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens, Nandalal has depicted a rooster, a smooth rendition in loose yet swift strokes, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the upper margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal's smaller sketches are testimony of his keen observation and empathy for the environment in which he lived. In this second sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal depicts a rooster, roughly rendered in dark contouring lines, coarse in character. The strong curvilinear strokes define the plumage and the long tail adding vitality to the form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal's sketches are testimony of the rich detailing of his observations, experiences and sojourns to various places. In this fourth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal sketches a rooster and a hen, studying the difference between the two, demarcated with sharp strokes. There are also small line drawing templates of a rooster and its crown. Nandalal also sketches a line drawing of a female figure holding a baby, roughly rendered in sharp outlines.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' twice, in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal's small sketches vastly vary in detailing, some drawn quickly with just a few lines, others executed with more elaborate characteristics from an analytical perspective. In this third sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal depicts a rooster, a quick line drawing rendered in swift, effortless strokes. He closely studies the the wattle of the rooster in a smaller template on the side.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal's exploration of delineating a line in different ways allowed him to experiment, adding rhythm and life to various forms. In this sixth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal depicts a rooster, a hen and a rabbit in simple line drawings, sparing much detail. He renders the sketches in a few quick strokes that convey their characteristic features and movements.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal preferred drawing from life, often sketching outdoors, the subject being nature studies, landscapes, figure drawings and birds and animals. Often the sketches were small in scale although invigorating with the rich detailing of the artist's observations, experiences and sojourns to various places. In this sketch, the fifth in the series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal depicts a line drawing of a hen, with a few confident strokes, that convey its movement and characteristic features.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top right-corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal had a firm belief that for the creation of art an intimate understanding of nature and its ways is imperative. The range of his artistic expression is seen in the changing Indian landscapes, varied images of nature and the portrayal of people and places. This sketch by him, the seventh in the series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, depicts a rooster, roughly rendered in long, loose strokes that define the contours of its body. He also studies it in another template on the side, as it pecks on food.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' twice, in Bengali along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal had a strong affinity for sketching, his subjects being the surrounding environs, people in their everyday life or anything that he found fascinating. In this eighth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal depicts a rooster pecking on its feathers, swiftly sketched in short strokes. He also depicts a rabbit lying on the ground in a simple line drawing in a smaller template.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' twice, in Bengali along the lower margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal's small sketches vastly vary in detailing, some drawn quickly with just a few lines, others executed with more elaborate characteristics from an analytical perspective. In this sketch, the ninth in the series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, Nandalal intently studies the head of a hen, a rooster and a rabbit, rendered in fine lines, delineated in a realistic representation.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal's smaller sketches are testimony of his keen observation and empathy for the environment in which he lived. This sketch by him, the last in the series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, depicts two roosters fighting, rendered in short, sharp strokes that are delineated in an illustrative manner.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has, in this monochromatic painting, emphasised the tones of the colour for precise and recognizable variations. In this tenth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of roosters and hens in the album, he has sketched a hen, rendered in swift, confident strokes of watercolour employing the dry brush technique to lend texture to the depiction.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-left corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal would make numerous sketches of aspects of the local environs on his travels. This first sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, depicts Gangdhara Machh , a freshwater fish abundantly found in Bengal. He renders the fish in fine lines, defining the contours of its slender body. Nandalal also sketches the top of the fish's head in a smaller template.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, 'Gangdhara Machh'.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Sketching and drawing were an integral part of Nandalal's daily activities and everything provided subject matter for the indefatigable artist. In this second sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, sketched at Rajmahal in Jharkhand, Nandalal depicts an eel, rendered in deep contouring lines. The light shading accentuates its texture and lends body to the robust form.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'N.L.B' and dated '3.11.28' below the sketch. There is an inscription that reads "Rajmahal". There is another inscription in Bengali that reads, "Pankal Machh" or Eel.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this third sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, sketched at Rajmahal in Jharkhand, Nandalal depicts a catfish. He renders the fish in smooth, fluid lines, defining the contours of its structure. The light shading and smudging accentuates the texture of its scales.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'N.L.Bose' and dated '3.11.28', along the left margin of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads "Rajmahal". There is another inscription in Bengali that reads, "lote machh" or Catfish.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: The fervent sketching of his surroundings, allowed Nandalal to meditate upon the elements of nature. In this fifth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal depicts a Trout, a freshwater fish, carefully rendered in fine, delicate lines. The light shading accentuates the texture of the scales on its body.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the top-left corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this fourth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, sketched at Rajmahal in Jharkhand, Nandalal depicts a catfish. He renders the fish in wiry lines, defining the structure of its body, sparing much detail. In a smaller template, he has also sketched the fish from the top.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'N.L.Bose' and dated '3.11.28' in the top-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription that reads "Rajmahal". There is another inscription in Bengali that reads, "Gete Machh" or Catfish.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this seventh sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal reproduces a crab, rendered in swift outlines, sparing much detail. The quick calligraphic strokes add rhythm and life to the water animal. Nandalal also sketches the underside of a crab, a rough rendition in a smaller template.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'N.L.B' and dated '10.12.1940' along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the sixth in the series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal has rendered a fish, in fluid, rhythmic outlines. The light shading accentuates the scales, partially depicted over its body.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal produced a series of sketches on postcard sized papers depicting the environs of Santiniketan and its surrounding areas. In this eighth sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal has rendered a catfish, a freshwater fish found abundantly in Bengal. He has executed the sketch in a few confident strokes that add vitality to the slender body.

metadata.inscription: Inscribed 'Tangra Machh' and dated '18.6.30', in Bengali in the bottom-left corner of the sketch. Also mentioned are the colours of the fish's body in Bengali, that translate to, 'Blood red and silver'.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the ninth in the series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal reproduces a catfish, sketched in short, sharp strokes. The pencil shading adds depth and body to the form of the fish.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. Inscribed 'Tangra Machh' below the sketch.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: In this sketch, the tenth in the series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal depicts several fishes in small detailed templates. He renders the forms in fine, fluid lines and carefully studies the nuances of their slender bodies. The light shading adds depth and volume to the depictions.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-left corner of the sketch. Also inscribed are the variety of fish in Bengali.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Sketching and drawing were an integral part of Nandalal's daily activities, and everything- from a monumental landscape to the tiniest insect- provided subject matter for the indefatigable artist. In this sketch he has rendered a line drawing of a grasshopper in delicate strokes that add life and vitality to the insect.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali below the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Ghoraphoring" or Grasshopper, in the bottom right-corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1
artworks.description: Nandalal has, in this monochromatic drawing, emphasised the use of the line for precise and recognizable variations. In this last sketch of a series of eleven sketches of aquatic life in the album, Nandalal depicts a freshwater fish, rendered in bold outlines of ink and watercolour, defining the contours of its body. The swift strokes add grace and vigour to the forms.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' and dated '21.5.1939' in Bengali beside the sketch.

artworks.title: A sketch from Sketch Book No.1

metadata.inscription: Dated '7th day of posh month' in Bengali along the right margin of the postcard with black ink. artworks.description: In this pencil sketch, Nandalal has reproduced several renditions of flower-motifs as executed on the Buddhist stupa relics in Bharhut, Madhya Pradesh, as the inscription indicates. artworks.description: In this pen and ink sketch, Nandalal has sketched a design (a stylised mango leaf motif consisting of various patterns) for Balucharee saree, rendered with linear, firm ink strokes, articulating the intricate design. He often made records of the ornamental carvings on historical buildings as Nandalal had a deep appreciation for the rich sculptural and architectural productions of ancient and medieval India and frequently incorporated elements from them into his works.

The inscription along the lower margin of the postcard is a repetition is same as above.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 5
artworks.description: Nandalal's exploration of the different ways of delineating a line allowed him to experiment with its varying forms adding rhythm, vigour and life to the form of the figure. The above sketch depicts the portrait of a man, the contours of his face have been delineated strongly, while the rest of the figure has been rendered in swift, short strokes.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 5
artworks.description: Nandalal had a strong affinity for sketching, his subjects being the surrounding environs, people in their everyday life or anything that he found fascinating. The artist understood the significance of the use of lines and experimented frequently in their execution from fine lines to being thick contouring lines. This sketch by him is the portrait of a man. The fluid handling of the line and the dark pencil strokes suggest the contours of the face, highlighting the facial features that have been rendered in an impressionistic manner.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

The fluid handling of the line suggests the modelling of the body and the facial features, which have been rendered in an impressionistic manner.

artworks.title: Architectural Design from Sketch Book No.6
artworks.description: Nandalal had a strong affinity for sketching, his subjects being the surrounding environs, people in their everyday life or anything that he found fascinating. His firm belief that for the creation of art an intimate understanding of the nature and its ways is imperative. The range of Nandalal's artistic expression can be seen in the changing Indian landscapes, his varied images of nature and the portrayal of people and places. Eminent artist A. Ramachandran in the book, 'Rhythms of India: The Art of Nandalal Bose' has made the following observation about Nandalal's drawings and sketches - "He made quick graphic impressions, often simplifying them to just few lines as he sought to understand the inherent structure of what he was seeing. At times he recorded objects in a more analytical way, while at others he transformed them into visual codes of pattern."

artworks.title: Architectural Design from Sketch Book No.6
artworks.description: Nandalal closely studied the ancient mural traditions of the Ajanta in 1905. He also picked up the nuances of mural paintings from his visits to the Bagh caves to copy the deteriorating frescoes in 1921. Nandalal undertook extensive studies to comprehend the diversity in form, essence and treatment that was employed through the centuries by artisans and architects in the Indian classical art, the folk arts and temple architecture. His rich insights of the classical art practices allowed him to experiment and blend with ease and spontaneity the elements of each in an astonishingly free manner. This sketch is an apt example where the artist has made a visual record of an elaborately ornate doorjamb with multiple rows depicting geometric and floral patterns from the Bagh caves, as inscribed by the artist. The doorjamb also depicts the motif of 'makara', a mythical creature, seen in many Hindu temples as an ornamental motif often sculpted onto the richly carved pillars and brackets.

metadata.inscription: The painting bears an abbreviated signature of the artist, 'NLB', followed by the date, '26/2/21' in English at the centre of the drawing with pencil. The drawing also bears an inscription which reads 'Bag Cave No. 4' in English, referring to the Bagh Caves of Madhya Pradesh, central India.

This sketch is an apt example where the artist has made a visual record of a pillar that supports the roof of the cave temples. This sketch is an apt example where the artist has made a visual record of a 'makara', a mythical creature, seen in many Hindu temples as an ornamental motif often sculpted onto the richly carved pillars and brackets. artworks.description: In this sketch, Nandalal has reduced the form of a building to a simple line drawing quickly rendered with a few strokes, sparing any details. The blunt texture of the pencil gives a impressionistic touch. As per the inscription, this drawing has been sketched during his 1921 visit to the Bagh caves, a group of rock-cut architectural monuments, in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali, that reads, "Bagh 3", in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal's drawings on postcards are spontaneous, done either with pen or brush and are basically linear. The above monochrome sketch by Nandalal is a quick rendition of three boat house sailing through the waves. The directional strokes lend perspective and convey the flow of wind and water. The illustration is executed with fluid pencil strokes, sparing much detail.

metadata.inscription: Dated '6.1.28' in English and signed 'Nanda' in Bengali in the centre of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that can be read as, 'Kawapura' (referring to the place) below the date.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a tree-laden landscape, probably a forest, with a group of people, scribbled briskly with wiry lines, sparing much detail. As the inscription suggests, this drawing was sketched during his 1921 visit to the Bagh caves, a group of rock-cut architectural monuments, in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, 'Bagh 4' in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: This sketch by Nandalal depicts two loaded donkeys with a herder amidst a barren, desolate landscape, rendered with a few smudged strokes. The expansive view resonates stillness and quietude. As per the inscription, Nandalal sketched the drawing on his way to Sardarpur, a town on the Malwa plateau in present-day Madhya Pradesh.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' and dated '4.1.21' in Bengali in the bottom-left corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Channe Barui, cow-dung collector returning back home. Way to Sardarpur", above the signature. There is another inscription in Bengali that reads, "Bagh 5", in the bottom-right corner.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched part of a hilly range, rendered in a minimalist fashion with few lines and smudged strokes, adding rhythm to the forms. The light shading lends depth to the hillocks. As per the inscription, on his way to the Bagh caves, Nandalal's tent was erected on this particular hill with a village settlement on the eastern side of the tent.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that roughly reads, "Village is on the eastern side of the tent. (Bagh caves)", in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is another inscription in Bengali that reads, "Bagh 6".

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here reproduced the foliage covered landscape of the Bagh caves with a few visitors, rendered with smudged strokes and light shading. The minute detailing of the leaves on the trees adds vivacity to the entire view. As per the inscription, the drawing was sketched during Nandalal's 1921 visit to the Bagh caves, a group of rock-cut architectural monuments, in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, 'Bagh 7', in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a village settlement by the river bank, roughly scribbled in quick, soft strokes of the pencil. The light shading lends depth to the trees and the ground. As per the inscription, the landscape has been sketched at Patisar, a village in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, 'Pratisar' (Patisar), in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a river bank with trees, rendered quickly with rough and bold strokes, adding vigour and life to the organic forms. The smudged texture lends a rugged effect to the calm terrain. As per the inscription, the drawing was sketched at Patisar, a village in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Patisar" (Patisar), in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a landscape, rendered with minimum lines, delineating to an illustrative manner. The gradation of light and dark strokes make up a great play of chiaroscuro. As per the inscription, written by Mukul Dey, (a student of Nandalal) the cross mark in the drawing probably denotes the place where Nandalal's mother's cremation took place.

metadata.inscription: Dated "8th November' 1917", along the bottom margin of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that roughly reads, "Nanda da's things being returned back to him- Mukul(Mukul Dey)", in continuation with the date. There is another inscription in Bengali that reads, "River named Mani, Kharagpur, Mother's memorial place.", below the date.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a trail of loaded donkeys treading on hilly terrain, rendered in bold and dark outlines, defining the contours of the frail bodies bearing weight. As per the inscription, the drawing was sketched in Kalimpong, a hill station in West Bengal, India.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that reads "Kalimgpong", in the bottom-right corner.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: The sketch above portrays an isolated hut amidst a bushy landscape, rendered in a few quick and wiry lines. Nandalal has approached the subject in a minimalistic manner, understanding the inherent structure and reproducing it in a simple form, sparing much detail.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched small huts by the sea shore, rendered in light, impressionistic strokes of the pencil. The expanse of the sky and the water body merge at the horizon, resonating a sense of calm and serenity.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal preferred drawing from life, often sketching outdoors with the subjects being life, nature studies, landscapes, figure drawings and animals. In the above sketch, Nandalal has rendered a tree trunk with a few, bold brush strokes suggesting the thickness of the tree. The strokes are executed in calligraphic fashion adding vigour and dynamism to the composition.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched the Gaibinath Temple, in Sultanganj, Jharkhand, located amidst a river over a small hill, rendered in soft, smudged strokes. The dark scribbling on the hill highlights the thick foliage and the slight shading gives a ripple effect in the otherwise still water.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'N.L.Bose' and dated '29 October, 1921', along the right margin of the sketch. There is another inscription in English that reads, "Gaibinath".

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal had a strong fascination for sketching nature, especially veteran trees that had some kind of spiritual significance. In this rough sketch he depicts a group of trees, their branches intertwined, in a cluster of wiry contouring lines while the coarse shading brings out the rugged texture of the tree trunk.

artworks.title: A Sketch from Sketch Book No. 7

metadata.inscription: There is another inscription in English that reads, 'Gaibinath' in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal here sketches the Tarakeshwar temple, in West Bengal, India. He renders the drawing in sharp lines, a quick study, delineated in the manner of an illustration.

metadata.inscription: There are two similar inscriptions in Bengali that read, "Tarakeshwar", along the right margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a palm tree, carefully studying its structure and character. The short, sharp strokes imbue the drawing with a certain energy. As per the inscription, the drawing has probably been sketched at Ilambazar, a town in the Birbhum district of West Bengal.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Ilambazaar", in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here rendered the sketch of the platform where Ramkrishna Paramhansa, a 19th century religious scholar and priest at the Dakshineshwar temple, in West Bengal, would meditate. Nandalal intently studies the structure and character of the Panchvati trees and their dangling branches that surround the seat, rendered in fluid contouring lines. The slight shading and smudging brings out a certain depth, enhancing the texture of the forms.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that roughly translates as, "Platform in Panchvati where Ramakrishna Paramhansa meditated", along the lower-margin of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched the hut in which Ramakrishna Paramhansa, a 19th century religious scholar and priest at the Dakshineshwar temple, in West Bengal, would meditate. Enclosed by trees and their dangling branches, Nandalal intently studies the character of the structure and renders it in thick and fluid contouring lines.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that roughly translates to, "Hut of Ramakrishna Paramhansa below the Panchvati trees", in the bottom-right corner of the image.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: As per the inscription, Nandalal has here sketched the trees in the Panchvati complex in the premises of the Dakshineshwar temple, in West Bengal. He studies the twisted and intertwined dangling branches, rendered in sharp flowing lines, defining the contours of the organic forms.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Dakshineshwar - Panchvati", in the bottom-right corner of the image.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: In the drawing above, Nandalal renders a landscape with a tree and bushes by a hillock, employing scribbled and wiry contouring lines, delineated in the manner of an illustration. It is a quick and rough rendition, sparing much detail.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: In this sketch, Nandalal renders the thatched huts of the rural landscape of Patisar, in present-day Bangladesh, where the zamindari of the Tagore family was head-quartered. It is a quickly executed drawing in swift, coarse strokes of the pencil.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '5.1.28', below the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Kaligram", below the signature. There is yet another inscription in Bengali that reads, "Pratisar"(Patisar).

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a small thatched hut on a hillock. He renders the drawing in a minimalistic fashion, with blunt scribbles and light shading. The rough texture, delineated in an illustrative manner, adds life and depth to the organic forms. As per the inscription, the drawing has been sketched at Kaligram Pargana, in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was head-quartered.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '6.1.28', in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Kaligram", along the signature. There is yet another inscription in Bengali that reads, "Pratisar" (Patisar).

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a rural settlement of thatched huts surrounded by trees and bushes, creating form out of a gradation of light and dark scribbles. The hasty and blunt strokes lend a rustic touch to the scene. This drawing has been sketched at Patisar, a village in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and inscribed "Pratisar" (Patisar), in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: In the sketch above Nandalal reproduces a village settlement rendered in dark, blunt outlines. The light and dark shading, a play of chiaroscuro, brings out the depth in the landscape. As per the inscription, this drawing was sketched at Patisar, a village in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in English that reads, "Patisar", in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: In the sketch above Nandalal portrays the banks of the Atrai River in West Bengal, dense with foliage. He renders the subject in smudged scribbles and shading, adding depth to the scene that has been executed in an impressionistic manner.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in English that reads, "Attrai River", in the bottom right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a thatched hut with a bullock cart from the region of Bhelva, Bihar. He renders the subject in fine, sharp outlines, sparing much detail. The gradation of light and dark strokes denotes the play of light and shade on the house.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '30 October 1917', in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in Bengali that roughly translates to, "Bhelva", below the signature.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a landscape of Gangtok in Sikkim. He renders the magnificent, densely forested region creating form out of smudges. The strong illustrative manner of the depiction, lends depth and vivacity to the whole view.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '2 May 1917', in the bottom-left corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Gangtok", below the signature.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a hut amidst palm trees on a hillock in Kharagpur, West Bengal. He renders the line drawing in bold and blunt outlines, using only a few strokes to depict the entire scene.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in English that reads, "Kharagpur", in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: In this sketch Nandalal studies two fishermen in their boat, rendered in strong, sharp outlines. The directional strokes lend perspective and convey the flow of wind and water. As per the inscription, the drawing was sketched at Kaligram, in present-day Bangladesh, where the Tagore family's zamindari was headquartered.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '5.1.28', in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Kaligram", below the signature.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a grocery shop opposite the house of artist Upendra Maharathi, a student of his, in Mayapur, West Bengal. He has reproduced the scene teeming with people in fine, sharp outlines. The minute detailing on the bamboo roof and leaves of the trees is a subtle touch by the artist.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '5.11.17', in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that roughly translates to, "Mayapur (opposite Upen's (Upendra Maharathi) house). Grocery shop made of Bamboo staves".

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched an expansive rural landscape of agriculture fields with animals and mud houses. He has rendered the drawing in simple outlines and bold pencil smudges, in a play of light and shade.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali that reads, "Gangtok", in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: A Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: Nandalal is known to have fervently sketched on postcard sized papers recording his surroundings. His small sketches vastly vary in detailing, some drawn quickly with just a few lines, others executed with more elaborate characteristics from an analytical perspective. This is another sketch in the series of temple lamps that Nandalal has depicted in this album, from his sojourns to various places across the country.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in Bengali, below the sketch that reads, "Udayan Uttarayan" or "Sunrise Sunset". There is another inscription in the bottom-right corner with pencil that reads, "Gurudev" referring to Rabindranath Tagore's title.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched the Kasht Harina Ghat at Munger, a district by the Ganges in Bihar. He uses a combination of ink and pencil to render the subject in fine outlines, in a minimalistic manner. The horizon, represented in smooth lines, lends a calm to the entire sketch.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '7.11.17', along the lower margin of the sketch. There is an inscription in English that reads, "Monghyr". There is yet another inscription in Bengali that roughly translates to "Munger, Kashto Harina Ghat", along the right margin.

artworks.title: Sketch Book No. 7
artworks.description: Nandalal has here sketched a monochrome landscape of a river surrounded by thick foliage. The smooth and dark rendition of scribbled and smudged textures, adds depth to the view. The light shading in the water and the gentle strokes for the shrubs, convey the effect of light breeze over the serene landscape.

artworks.title: A Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: In this delicate ink sketch, Nandalal renders a waterpipe or hookah commonly smoked across South Asia. This is one among many such sketches of hookas from various places that Nandalal has documented in this album, detailing and recording regional variations in its designs.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali and dated '17.11.1930' in English in the bottom-right corner of the sketch.

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8

His small sketches vastly vary in detailing, some drawn quickly with just a few lines, others executed with more elaborate characteristics from an analytical perspective. In the sketch above Nandalal depicts a temple lamp from Southern India, as the inscription suggests. He has recreated its intricate design, including a detailed inset of the ornamental bird motif at its head.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in English that reads, "Southern Indian Lamp".

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: Nandalal has, in this sketch, reproduced an ornately-carved decorative object, probably a metallic door knocker. He had a deep appreciation for indigenous designs and motifs and often made visual records of these, wherever he encountered them.

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: In this sketch Nandalal renders several designs of ornamental architectural brackets. Done quickly, these were meant to serve as reference sketches.

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: In this image Nandalal has traced the designs of two ornaments, probably bangles, using the technique of frottage - where a pencil is rubbed on paper that has been placed over a textured surface to get an impression of the pattern below. The sketch illustrates Nandalal's impulse to imitate the motif in its original form to enrich his knowledge of design and ornamental work.

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: In this intricate sketch by Nandalal, he depicts a stambha from Nepal, as the inscription suggests. The symbolic pillar is part of both Hindu and Buddhist mythology, where it could represent among other things, a cosmic pillar connecting heaven and the earth or a monolithic memorial pillar, topped with a lotus shaped capital and animal sculptures.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in English that reads, "From Nepal, 'Stambha'".

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: In this delicate ink sketch, Nandalal renders a waterpipe or hookah commonly smoked across South Asia. This is one among many such sketches of hookas from various places that Nandalal has documented in this album, detailing and recording regional variations in its designs.

metadata.inscription: There is an inscription in English in the bottom-right corner that reads, 'Nepali Hooka'.

metadata.inscription: Inscribed 'Birbhum' in English along the lower margin of the sketch, referring to the place it was sketched at.

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8

artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8

Here he renders a scene from Tanda, a small town close to the Bagh Caves in Madhya Pradesh. artworks.title: Sketch from Sketch Book No. 8
artworks.description: In this pencil sketch, Nandalal has portrayed the detailed design for a wood and rope chair along with several smaller sketches of designs of wooden legs of chairs and charpoys.

artworks.description: In this sketch Nandalal renders several designs of ornamental bases of pillars from his travels across the country. Done quickly, these were meant to serve as reference sketches.
