artworks.title: Clown
artworks.description: The visuals structure in Zharotia's works have been compared to Japanese Haikus, with his sparse use of figures on flat color surfaces equivalent to the musical notes that hang isolated in the space. His works, like those of the western expressionists as Jean Miro and Paul Klee have a playful element with a softness of painted forms and playful placement of human, animate and inanimate objects in his compositions create a childlike curiosity while viewing his paintings. But even in the presence of this playful element his works have strong suggestion to the society like a dismantled idea of power and authority attributed to masculinity. The duality of life and the imagined life, that is the experience and the imagination can be seen reflected in his works. His paintings one can see unusual spaces, almost surreal which are much beyond the common places we see around. The play of light and shadow that can be seen in his works is also not confined to any physical laws, much like the subjects of his paintings.

artworks.title: Through The Darkness Floods
artworks.description: K. K. Hebbar was drawn to impressionism, although it was Indian classical art that remained a ceaseless source of inspiration. His early paintings – landscapes and figural compositions in the academic style – disciplined his hand and mind and led him towards his own style.Inspired by Ananda Coomaraswamy’s discourses, Hebbar began exploring his creativity through the forms of traditional Indian art found in Jain manuscripts, Rajput and Mughal miniatures and the murals at Ajanta. In his drawings and paintings, Hebbar harmoniously blended the traditional form with elements of surrealist and abstract art. Strongly inspired by Amrita Sher-Gil’s manner of expressing her vision of the East through Western techniques, Hebbar’s inclination lay toward Western art, and to explore it further he left for Europe in 1949.

artworks.description: Anju's work concerns with the collective subconscious that forms out of the network of workings of the human mind. On this subconscious level all identities overlap or merge and form a collective image. But when under pressure these surface as solid blocks of violent egoistic outbursts. It is this outbursts which become a part of Anju's canvases, where she tries to find the link between the mysterious and the apparent, the unknown and the known, the Godly and the human. In this painting, the artist has depicted a veiled woman carrying a basket on her head, rendered in fluid strokes of watercolour in tonal variation adding grace and fine lines of ink delineating the contours of the figure.

metadata.inscription: Dated '11.12.48' in English in the bottom-right corner of the sketch. There are two inscriptions in English which can be read as, 'Jaipure Congress' and Jhandachawk'.

artworks.title: Animal Instinct
artworks.description: Upendra Maharathi uses Bengal school mannerism and romanticism to blend it with new themes, subjects and geometric simplifications. In the above painting title ‘Animal Instinct’, the artist has depicted a dagger killing the spirit of animals, rendered with the shades of oil colours in tonal variation creating depth in the composition.

artworks.title: THE BARE TRUTH
artworks.description: Upendra Maharathi uses Bengal school mannerism and romanticism to blend it with new themes, subjects and geometric simplifications. In the above painting titled ‘the bare truth’ depicts a bare body of a man carried away by three different people, probably having some significant meaning. The subject has been rendered with the use of warm colour over the background having the shades of blue.

artworks.title: MOUNTAIN
artworks.description: In this watercolor sketch, he has depicted a serene landscape with mountains and a man with a child standing near a river. Rendered with the light shades of watercolour and loose, quick strokes of pen delineating the forms.

artworks.title: TOY ELEPHANT WITH RIDER
artworks.description: Upendra Maharathi had made sketches of nature and people and used simple bold lines to capture any basic form. The above sketch by him depicts a toy elephant with a rider, executed with thick, bold brush strokes delineating the forms.

artworks.title: Temple

artworks.title: Gandhi Profile
artworks.description: Maharathi was an admirer of Mahatma Gandhi and made several of his portraits and sketches in his book, Gandhi: The Super Star (Line Drawings). He made 39 sketches of Gandhi in his various moods. The above portrait is a perceptible representation of Mahatma Gandhi in deep thought, rendered with smooth, fluid brush strokes articulating the contours and highlighting his facial features.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Man
artworks.description: The National gallery of Modern Art has in its collection, a number of portraits by Maharathi, which are mostly of eminent personalities and Indian martyrs. This one is a rare portrait painting of a man. The sketch has been swiftly executed in soft smudged, pencil strokes that suggest the contours of the face, highlighting the facial features and depth and light in the composition.

artworks.title: Gandhi Profile
artworks.description: Maharathi was an admirer of Mahatma Gandhi and made several of his portraits and sketches in his book, Gandhi: The Super Star (Line Drawings). He made 39 sketches of Gandhi in his various moods. The above portrait is a perceptible representation of Mahatma Gandhi in profile with a smile, rendered with smooth, fluid brush strokes articulating the contours, and bringing about a corporeality of form and substance.

artworks.title: To Deceive
artworks.description: Maharathi uses Bengal school mannerism and romanticism to blend it with new themes, subjects and geometric simplifications. The entire iconography seems to have transposed from the Ajanta to the above painting. Maharathi still uses a very fine boundary line that comes form the classical iconography that reoccurs in the Buddhist tradition of Ajanta and Bagh cave paintings, also the eyes, eyebrows and lips come from the same source. Maharathi is trying to link tradition with modernity andis trying to bring semblance to the analogy between what was there and what could be done now.

artworks.title: Images in Rocks
artworks.description: Maharathi has a series of paintings that he has titled 'Images in Rocks'. He often chose to paint the images that were accidentally formed by the creative formation of rocks. In the above painting the rock formations look like unidentified figures against bright background of green and yellow merging with blue.

artworks.title: Jay Prakash Narain
artworks.description: Deeply impressed and influenced by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian Independence movement the artist paid his respect by telling their stories through his paintings. He made a series of realistic portraits of many of India's martyrs. The collection of NGMA has a number of portraits of eminent freedom fighters such as Lal Bahadur Shastri, Lala Lajpat Rai, Sardar Patel among other. This one is a portrait of Jay Prakash Narain.

metadata.inscription: Dated '31.10.66' in Hindi vertically in the bottom-right corner of the painting . The painting also bears an inscription in Hindi which reads 'Jay Prakash Narain'.

artworks.title: Lord Buddha
artworks.description: The image has a reference to the life of Buddha. It is said that during the period of austerities when Buddha was seeking enlightenment, he had to struggle with many obstacles designed to disturb his meditation. This delicately painted image visualises a man rising above overwhelming impediments. The artist uses a stylised language to depict the scene.

artworks.title: Sagar Surrenders at the Feet of Shri Rama

artworks.title: Earth Question's the Mountain
artworks.medium: Chinese black ink on rice paper
artworks.description: This painting belongs to a series of monochromatic ink paintings by Upendra Maharathi. These compositions were stripped to the bare minimum where only a few strokes of ink were employed to create natural forms in an effortless approach. In the above sketch, he has depicted a mountain forming a shape of a human, with a range of strokes in tonal variations capturing the rhythm and pattern of the image.

artworks.title: Mountain Questions

artworks.title: Bodhi Tree
artworks.description: The above oil painting is a naturalistic representation of the sacred spot in Bodhgaya, showing the Bodhi tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment. He has painted the subject with shades of colours in tonal variation, conveys a sense of sanctity and serenity in this painting.

artworks.title: Images in Rocks
artworks.description: Maharathi has a series of paintings that he has titled 'Images in Rocks'. He often chose to paint the images that accidentally formed by a creative formation of rocks. In the above painting the rock formations look like Devotees kneeling down in reverence beneath a large figure of Buddha with a distinct usnisa (Top Knot). Rectangular strokes of paint in blue and white form the large mound of rocks, whereas the thinly applied blue paint in the sky merges with the yellow in the background.

artworks.title: Images in Rocks: Indra and Indrani on Airavata
artworks.description: Maharathi has a series of paintings that he has titled 'Images in Rocks'. He often chose to paint the images that accidentally formed by a creative formation of rocks. artworks.title: Kanchanjunga
artworks.description: In the above oil painting Maharathi has depicted the famous mount ‘Kanchanjunga’ bathed in the warm sunlight against a blue grey sky. The artist has built up a foundation of cool colours and with loose brush strokes he adds golden yellow to finish the rising peak of Mt. Kanchanjunga.

artworks.title: Images in Nature
artworks.description: Maharathi often chose to paint the images that accidentally formed by a creative formation of nature. The above painting ‘Images in nature’ depicts the artist observation of nature, in which a human figure emerging within the trunk of a tree and stands in front of a kneeling figure of a woman. He has painted the subject in its pure form and filled in the large areas of the painting with thick brush strokes.

artworks.title: Earth Question's the Mountain
artworks.description: Maharathi often chose to paint the images that accidentally formed by a creative formation of rocks. In the above painting the rock formations look like a huge lion like face with its paws in the front manifests the mountain, and a human like form which has grown from within the gleaming golden earth with a gesturing hand asking question to the mountain. He creates a strong diagonal by juxtaposing the white and blue mountain on either side of the composition and softly blends the blue green sky while thick strokes of paint materialize the rest of the painting.

artworks.title: Wait
artworks.description: Upendra Maharathi uses Bengal school mannerism and romanticism to blend it with new themes, subjects and geometric simplifications. In the above oil painting, he has depicted a woman patiently waiting in the front porch of her house rendered with warm colors.

artworks.description: Maharathi was an admirer of Mahatma Gandhi and made several of his portraits and sketches in his book, Gandhi: The Super Star (Line Drawings). artworks.description: Deeply impressed and influenced by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian Independence movement the artist paid his respect by telling their stories through his paintings. He made a series of realistic portraits of many of India's martyrs. The collection of NGMA has a number of portraits of eminent freedom fighters such as Lal Bahadur Shastri, Lala Lajpat Rai, Sardar Patel among others. This one is a portrait of Rabindranath Tagore.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Hore's work are filled by humanist eye, inclination towards empathy, and his communist ideology. Tension in lines and emaciating figures were significant in most of his works. He was driven with the feeling of anguished and suffering of the poor. The overall impression one gets from Somnath’s works is the depth of poverty he has starved in. He used knives and red-hot rods to cut and burn into a piece of clay, which then provided the basis for a cement mould that would shape and scar the paper pulp. He moulded the white paper to form wound-like gashes, and stained them with red blood-like pigment. The haunted imagery, blisters of the restrained figures made him poignant among others. Hore stated,' I do not make pictures, I make 'wounds' indeed.

artworks.title: Santhal Family
artworks.description: Ramkinkar Baij was a reclusive modernist artist who always remained on the fringes of the art market. He took a great interest in human figures, body language and in the general human drama. Modern Western art and pre and post-classical Indian art were his main points of reference. Although primarily known for his expressionistic sculpture, he was also a gifted painter. The sense of rhythm that his sculpture was noted for is manifested brilliantly in his paintings and sketches. His works in the Kalighat tradition interconnected with Cubism to achieve an unusual personal idiom. Both his sculpture and his paintings are unprompted and bold.

artworks.description: A sensitive artist, Reddy evolved a unique vision of his own, creating complex compositions, realistic and expressionistic portraits, still-lifes and impressionistic landscapes. His later works are abstract, often revealing a tantric influence with folk motifs and symbols, and a synthesis of almost contrary forms. An excellent draughtsman, Reddy’s lines have an even flow, rarely changing in thickness or intensity. He was also trained in mural design and was acquainted with the Rajput and Pahari miniature styles.

artworks.title: Harvest, 1995
artworks.description: A self-taught artist Arpana Caur has excelled in the numerous genres of art, which include painting, sculpture, print-making and installations. She was born in 1954, Delhi, was raised by her mother and graduated with a degree in literature. Driven by her intense desire to paint she dropped the idea of having a career in teaching and is now one of the most distinguished Indian artists. Caur has exhibited her works in eighteen solo shows and nine national and international exhibitions. She has received many awards including the All India Fine Arts and Crafts Society (AIFACS) Award in 1985, a Gold medal at the Sixth Triennale- India and a commendation certificate at the Algiers Biennale in 1986. Arpana Caur was inspired by the leading women artists of the country, particularly, Amrita Sher-Gil whose works were dominant with the portrayal of women with a certain feminist perspective. Arpana Caur's own style is very individualistic devoid of any sexual expressions and erotica though they have a strong presence of women oriented issues. Her feminist approach to painting is very symbolic and suggested by the repeated motifs of the cloth, thread and scissors that appear in her works. These symbols mark a direct comment on the commonly believed notions of women's contribution to society. Inspired by Pahari miniatures her works are imbued with mysticism, religion, devotional poetry and religious thoughts. Her series of works on Sufi saints and themes particularly about women frequent as subjects.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Coachman (Bengal Company Style)
Priest with Elokeshi, Kalighat
artworks.description: In front of you is an archetypal 19th century Kalighat painting. It is titled ‘Priest with Elokeshi’. Kalighat paintings emerged from the tradition of patachitra. Patachitras were drawings on cloth scrolls used by travelling storytellers in rural Bengal. Each section of the cloth was called a pat which gave their creators the name patua. According to art historians, patuas were not exactly a separate community and often included potters, stoneworkers and carpenters. In the 19th century, Bengal saw migration from rural areas to the up and coming urban centre of Calcutta. Among the migrants were artisans such as the patuas. Many of these patuas settled themselves around the popular pilgrim destination of the temple of Kalighat. Thematically, the paintings were divided into Oriental and Occidental. The former depicted gods, goddesses, mythological characters as well as scenes from religious Hindu texts. The Occidental variety featured secular and civil themes. These could be satirical such as those depicting the Bengali babu, or celebrate the heroism of Rani Lakshmi Bai and Tipu Sultan. Some, such as ‘Priest with Elokeshi’, depicted contemporary developments. Elokeshi was raped by the head priest of a temple and killed by her husband. Young Elokeshi’s plight echoes across time through the Kalighat paintings.

artworks.description: Somnath Hore is remembered because of his creativity and excellence in inventing new media of printing techniques. Though Gaganendranath Tagore was the father of Indian printmaking, Hore made his presence felt immensely in it. The depiction of the sufferings and atrocities of the poor and the anguished figures with a placement of soaring birds and animals occupy most of the art works produced. His experiments with various print-making techniques and mediums such as etching, intaglio and lithographs led him to develop a new medium called 'Pulp-prints'.

artworks.title: Bosom - Friends
artworks.description: Kalam Patua was born into the Patua community, the community of scroll painters, in 1962. He is the pioneer to the contemporary form of Kalighat Painting. He revived the traditional art form of Kalighat painting from its conventional patachitra style to a more contemporary subject, form and style. His subjects are often symbolic of the happenings around the city life, the elites, often induced with humor, satire, idea and thought provoking attitude. The subtle use of colours in different hues and tones, bold lines are characteristic style of Kalam Patuaâ??s Kalighat style paintings. This painting reflects the genderqueer identities in the contemporary society.

artworks.title: Cities
artworks.description: Zarina in her works, adheres to the use of geometry and structural purity, which she drew from her formal education in mathematics and architecture. In the above print from the series 'Cities', Zarina has rendered the layout of a high-rise building representing New York city, in her signature minimalist style. She depicts her subjects in abstract compositions, reminiscing a life left behind.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Zarina' and dated '2003' along the lower margin of the print. There is an inscription in Urdu that can be translated as 'New York' along the right margin of the print. There is an inscription in English that reads, 'City-IV' along the lower margin of the print.

artworks.title: Amul Dairy Founder
artworks.description: Among the many portraits of known Indian personalities that Elisabeth Brunner and her mother painted during their stay, after their coming back to India in 1938, was this one - of the founder of the Amul Dairy of Anand. Brunner painted many portraits of the renowned personalities like Jawaharlal Nehru, Sarojini Naidu, Indira Gandhi and many more.

artworks.title: Toda Girl
artworks.description: Among the many paintings that Elisabeth Brunner and her mother painted during their travel in India is this one - a beautiful portrait of a girl of the Toda tribe of southern India. Brunner's works are in an extensive range with paintings of landscapes, people, street life and many portraits, along with those of renowned personalities like Jawaharlal Nehru, Sarojini Naidu, Indira Gandhi and many others.

artworks.title: Sir V. T. Krishnamachari, Dewan of Baroda
artworks.description: Among the many portraits of known Indian personalities that Elisabeth Brunner and her mother painted during their stay, after their coming back to India in 1938, is this one of Sir V.T. Krishnamachari, Diwan of Baroda. This portrait painted by Brunner is supposed to be made by her during her stay in Baroda when the Maharaja of Baroda had invited them to paint a collection exclusively for the Baroda museum and Art Gallery.

artworks.title: The Ancient Gate Of Jhalawar Town
artworks.description: Elizabeth Sass Brunner mainly painted landscapes, still life and street paintings throughout her travels in and around India. This painting is an example of one such work, depicting a landscape of Jhalawar street with a historic entrance gate to the town.

artworks.title: Dehradoon Seen From Mussoorie
artworks.description: Elizabeth Sass Brunner painted many landscapes with mountains, forests,, monuments and street life. throughout her travel to India from Italy with her daughter. She visited many lands in search new paths of life and noted the spirit of the lands and the people she met in her paintings. After the World War II the Brunner along with her daughter shifted to the north of India where they also had their own cottage in Nainital. This landscape showing the eve lit Dehradoon is an expression with the colors and the bold strokes she has used in it.

artworks.title: Autumn Leaf Creepers on Trees
artworks.description: The image is that of a beautiful landscape showing trees in a forest. Elizabeth Sass Brunner painted many such landscapes with mountains, forests,, monuments and street life. This painting is one of her paintings done during her travel to India from Italy, while she along with her daughter visited many lands in search new paths of life.

artworks.title: Tagore's Historic Boat of Chandranagar
artworks.description: This landscape with historic boat of Tagores is made by Elizabeth Sass Brunner. Both the mother and Daughter artist duo came to India from Hungary in 1930 upon the invitation of the noble laureate Rabindranath Tagore. Elizabeth Sass Brunner was know for her landscapes with brushstrokes reflecting her eternal spiritual journey that was seeking throughout her travels in India and beyond, while her daughter was known for the portraits she made of major Indian personalities. This landscape painting too reflects the similar spirit of her journey to Chandranagar with vivid colors and brushstrokes creating the mystic sky.

artworks.title: The Smaller Blue Grotto
artworks.description: In the works of artists of Society of Spiritual Artists, light played an important role as a source of spiritual experience. Elizabeth Sass Brunner also seems to have an influence of this style which quite a lot reflects in this landscape painting of hers.

artworks.title: Gurudev Painting (Series: A Day with Gurudev), 1931
Harmonious Sicilian Mountains With Giant Rocks
artworks.description: Elizabeth Sass Brunner's work had a mystic character reflecting her journey of spirituality and finding her inner self. The Brunners, the artist mother and daughter duo started their journey around the world in search new paths of life. They first went to Italy, then to Sicily and then reached to India via Alexandria. This landscape was painted in Sicily. It shows a mystic play of light and dense colors a characteristic of Sass Brunner's works.

artworks.title: The Mountain of Sicily
artworks.description: The landscape is an apt example of mystic play of colours and light to create a eternal and spiritual experience which is a characteristic of Elizabeth Sass Brunner's works. She travelled to India in search of the same spiritual goals and a new path of life that reflects in all her works.

artworks.title: Self Portrait
artworks.description: Elizabeth Brunner became popular as a portrait painter as she made portraits of many prominent personalities who contributed to the national movement. she was also invited by many Maharajas to make portraits and add on to their collection. This work of hers is a self portrait depicting her caracter as an intense artist.

artworks.title: Tagore A Spiritual Body
artworks.description: The painting depicts the portrait of Rabindranath Tagore as a Spiritual being. The illuminating hues and application of the colour used, shows the spiritual aspect of Tagore's personality.

artworks.title: A Country Youth from Srirangapattnam
artworks.description: This work by Elizabeth Brunner is one among her many portraits of rural people that she painted during her travels in India. Apart from painting great personalities and portraits of Maharajas and national spokesmen, she also excelled in painting the rural people and country life. The portrait reflects the brilliant ability of the artist to capture the characters of the people she painted in bold quick strokes and a dense color pallete. Also the medium is quite indicative of her style of quickly capturing the imagery of her journey.

artworks.title: Spinning Expression
artworks.description: This painting is one among the many portraits of great personalities that Elizabeth Brunner painted during her travel and stay in India. The Image shows Gandhiji Spinning the Charkha. It is a very photographic capture of the personality's act of spinning the cotton yarn that the artist could achieve in this work of hers.

artworks.title: Professor Ythone Noguchi (?)
artworks.description: Between the years 1935 to 1937 the mother and daughter artist duo, Elisabeth Sass Brunner and Elisabeth Brunner travelled to Japan and exhibited their painting painted in India as well as Hungary there. They also travelled around Japan and were influenced by the land and the art there especially The sea and Fuji. It is during this span, Elizabeth Brunner painted the portrait of Professor Ythone Noguchi .

artworks.title: Four Aspects Of The Moon
artworks.description: This work by Elizabeth Sass Brunner depicts the four aspects of the moon. With the aspects of the moon used as a metaphor for women, the artist shows four nude women in different color tones to represent the four different aspects.

artworks.title: Sadhu
artworks.description: Portrait of the Sadhu is one among many portraits of rural people that Elizabeth Brunner painted during her travels in India. Apart from painting great personalities and portraits of Maharajas and national spokesmen, she also excelled in painting the rural people and country life. The portrait reflects the brilliant ability of the artist to capture the characters of the people she painted in bold quick strokes and a dense color pallete. Also the medium is quite indicative of her style of quickly capturing the imagery of her journey.

artworks.title: Portrait of Mrs. Sadek
artworks.description: Elizabeth Brunner became popular as a portrait painter in India. She made many portraits of great personalities, contributors to the national movement, royalties as well as rural people. The portrait of Mrs Sadek is among the many portraits she made during her stay in India.

artworks.title: Light Of The Night
artworks.description: Elizabeth Sass Brunner was a Hungarian Artist born in 1889 in Budapest. She lived and travelled in India extensively on pilgrimage tours with an artistic interest. She along with her daughter Elizabeth Brunner came to India in the year 1930 in search of a new path in life. Both the mother and daughter duo became the respected figures in Indian artistic life with their art subjects concentric on the life and spirit of India. Throughout their travel in India together they painted landscapes, mountains, forests, monuments and people along with major Indian personalities being received by Ravindranath Tagore, several Maharajas and also many prominent Indian spokesmen.

artworks.title: Bopaya Pagoda, 1956
artworks.description: The work is one among the series of paintings based on Buddhist theme, by the artist Elizabeth Brunner, created between the years 1955 to 1957, while she travelled on the pilgrimage tour. She visited and painted the holy shrines of Buddhism and Buddha images in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. It is done in the medium of oil on a palm leaf mat.

artworks.title: The Dream Of Maya Devi (Pagan)
artworks.description: The work is one among the series of paintings based on Buddhist theme, by the artist Elizabeth Brunner, created between the years 1955 to 1957, while she travelled on the pilgrimage tour. She visited and painted the holy shrines of Buddhism and Buddha images in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. It is done in the medium of oil on a palm leaf mat. It depicts one of the important themes of Buddhism when Maya Devi, the mother of Siddhartha, dreams of the four heavenly deities carried her to lake Anotatta in Himalayas and she sees the white elephant. Here we can see the four deities carrying her and she dressed in heavenly clothes.

artworks.title: In The Heart Of Pinda Cave
artworks.description: The work is one among the series of paintings based on Buddhist theme, by the artist Elizabeth Brunner, created between the years 1955 to 1957, while she travelled on the pilgrimage tour. She visited and painted the holy shrines of Buddhism and Buddha images in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. The painting is done in the medium of oil on a palm leaf mat and brilliantly gives the essence of the Pindaya cave which is an important pilgrimage site for Buddhist in Burma and an attractively unusual visual sight for tourists with thousands of Buddha images in various styles.

She visited and painted many holy shrines of Buddhism in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. The work is done in the medium of oil on palm leaf mat.

artworks.title: Buddhist Deity
artworks.description: The work is one of the beautiful drawings of a Buddhist deity. It is one among the series of paintings done by the artist while on the pilgrimage tour, with her artist daughter, visiting and painting the holy shrines of Buddhism in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. The work is done on the medium of oil on palm leaf mat.

artworks.title: Standing Buddha
artworks.description: The work depicts the image of the Standing Buddha. It is one among the series of 12 paintings entitled "Buddha's Enlightenment". This series was one of the greatest undertaking by the artist painted in the last period of the of her life span, till her death due to pneumonia in 1950. So most the paintings in this series are done between 1941 when she returned back to India from England till her death in 1950.

artworks.title: Buddha In Bhumi Spareha Mudra

She visited and painted the holy shrines of Buddhism in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. The work is done in the medium of oil on palm leaf mat.

artworks.description: Among the many portraits of known Indian personalities that Elizabeth Brunner and her mother painted during their travel in India like Jawaharlal Nehru, Sarojini Naidu, Indira Gandhi and many more, is this portrait of Krishna Baba, painted realistically.

It is one among the series of Buddha paintings done by the artist while on the pilgrimage tour, with her artist daughter, visiting and painting the holy shrines of Buddhism in India, Nepal, Myanmar (Burma), Sri Lanka and Thailand. The work is done on the medium of oil on palm leaf mat.

artworks.title: Father, Mother And Child

artworks.title: Feet Of Buddha

artworks.title: For Rohit Khosla, Delhi, 1989, Film
artworks.description: Even in his commercial photographs, Prabuddha injected a unique and creative spirit which signalled a major breakthrough in the field of advertising photography. This photograph by him belongs to the campaign for designer Rohit Khosla. Prabuddha's fashion imagery too, was marked by the simplicity that pervades his personal works.

artworks.title: Buddhist boy in Ranbirpura, Ladakh, 1995, Film
artworks.description: His book on Ladakh (2000) was the outcome of Prabuddha's long drawn affair with the place which he preferred to describe as 'a path' and 'not a mere destination'. The works in this series bring out the humbled faces of the people subjected to the extreme elements of nature. The sheer expanse and starkness of the topography and climate of the place seems unforgiving on the surface but is immensely gratifying in the spiritual sense. In the same way, this series is about unexpected revelations and connections. Ladakh revealed to Prabuddha a duality of contrasting qualities in terms of its people and its landscape.

artworks.title: Longing 19, 2005, Digital
artworks.description: Longing was Prabuddha's ongoing series when his untimely demise occurred. The series can be considered his most personal and intimate body of work. It represents his memories and experiences of the everyday. The photographs suggest a yearning for the familiar and the lived. The viewer feels like they are privy to the artist's private moments. A voyeuristic gaze from beyond accompanies a feeling of belonging from within owing to the intimate composition of the picture. A number of images from the Longing series have a misty filter over them. The photographed subject and the viewer are separated by this textured filter, creating an illusion of distance in time and space. The images contain a mood of languishing and lounging. The works are an amalgamation of sensuosity and meditativeness. What he knew, what was familiar, what moved him, what he treasured, what he felt, what is now but obscure memories chronicled together to articulate his desires and longing.

artworks.title: Laila Rouass, Delhi, 1996, Film
artworks.description: Prabuddha masterfully handles the thin line between private and public space. His vision is articulated through his pictures where the viewer is invited into the subject's space. Whether transient or intimate, the connections established between Prabuddha and his subject were always impactful. This particular photographic portrait features the model and actress, Laila Rouass. The ease exuded by the artist's subjects conveys a long standing familiarity between them but in many cases, this was achieved through a brief yet intense encounter.

artworks.title: Altar, Braganza House, Chandor, Goa, 2007, Digital
artworks.description: Prabuddha's last book Edge of Faith (2009) defined the life he led in his later years. What began as an attempt to document his Catholic neighbours in Goa eventually led to the exploration of the idiosyncrasies of the larger community. He captured the myriad faces of the community, the interiors of their houses, their rituals and their religious spaces. The old world spaces have a weighty atmosphere pervaded by a melancholic and nostalgic mood. The people are photographed in their familiar environs sans any choreography.

artworks.title: Procession of Tails, Sé Cathedral, Old Goa, 2009, Digital
artworks.description: Prabuddha's last book Edge of Faith (2009) defined the life he led in his later years. What began as an attempt to document his Catholic neighbours in Goa eventually led to the exploration of the idiosyncrasies of the larger community. He captured the myriad faces of the community, the interiors of their houses, their rituals and their religious spaces. The old world spaces have a weighty atmosphere pervaded by a melancholic and nostalgic mood. The people are photographed in their familiar environs sans any choreography.

artworks.title: Longing 9, 2006, Digital
artworks.description: Longing was Prabuddha's ongoing series when his untimely demise occurred. The series can be considered his most personal and intimate body of work. It represents his memories and experiences of the everyday. The photographs suggest a yearning for the familiar and the lived. The viewer feels like they are privy to the artist's private moments. A voyeuristic gaze from beyond accompanies a feeling of belonging from within owing to the intimate composition of the picture. A number of images from the Longing series have a misty filter over them. The photographed subject and the viewer are separated by this textured filter, creating an illusion of distance in time and space. The images contain a mood of languishing and lounging. The works are an amalgamation of sensuosity and meditativeness. What he knew, what was familiar, what moved him, what he treasured, what he felt, what is now but obscure memories chronicled together to articulate his desires and longing.

artworks.title: Press photographers waiting for a dignitary.
artworks.description: This series of photographs affords glimpses into the life of Indian press photographers as a community. The camaraderie between photographers of earlier years is very much in evidence. The personal element is clear from the carefree group photographs and the social evenings spent enjoying each others’ company. These images also document the close access to dignitaries enjoyed by the photographers and how it was progressively limited over the years eventually leading to the regulated and posed photo-op. In this particular image from the 1950s, press photographers can be seen waiting for a dignitary. Seen in the front is Homai Vyarawalla.

artworks.title: Captain Ram Charan Singh who composed the patriotic song "Kadam kadam Badhaye Ja", plays the violin for Gandhiji at the Harijan Colony, 1945
artworks.description: Kulwant Roy’s photographs capture the solidarity and determination of Congress leaders to secure the release of the three officers of the Indian National Army undergoing a court-martial and the suspension of their trials in 1945. Its leaders, beginning with Mahatma Gandhi and including Sardar Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru and Sarojini Naidu, are seen in a series of morale-boosting meetings with the soldiers, as Capt. Ram Singh, composer of the rousing “Kadam kadam badhaye ja”, plays the violin. The flags of the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League flew side by side in a wave of protests, the last time such unanimity would ever be seen.

artworks.title: Group photo taken after the inauguration ceremony show : Maharajas of Patiala, Kapurthala, Jind, Maler Kotla, Faridkot, kalsia along with Mr. U.P. Menon Secretary States Ministry.
artworks.description: This series of photographs by Kulwant Roy documents the integration of the former Princely states into the Union of India. Two separate occasions are recorded in these pictures: the inauguration of PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union) in Patiala in July 1948; and that of the Greater Rajasthan Union in Jaipur in March 1949. Sardar Patel appears in many of them, his presence austere in the lavish surroundings, yet possessed of an ease of equality.

artworks.title: Workers and Pay Van at Bhakra Nangal 1950
artworks.description: This series of photographs by Kulwant Roy documents the building of the Bhakra-Nangal Dam in the 1950s to harness the waters of the Sutlej for electricity and irrigation schemes that would benefit millions. In most pictures, the soon-to-be epic proportions of the dam are viewed on the scale of the human beings building it. This, then, is the story that is told in these photographs, the building of a nation through the unremitting toil of its citizens, no matter the scale of that toil. The images that we see are rooted in the climate of the times, the beliefs in development through industrial growth and the harnessing of science and technology.

artworks.title: Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto at the Indo-Pak talks during the Shimla Summit, 1972
artworks.description: This series of photographs by Kulwant Roy documents the post-Nehruvian era when Indira Gandhi became Prime Minister. A tumultuous time for the young country, it was trying to manage its international relations and formulate a foreign policy with respect to its South Asian neighbours. In this particular photograph, Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto are seen together during the Simla Summit of 1972 when the historic Simla Agreement was signed.

artworks.title: Protest Rally
artworks.description: Kulwant Roy's images afford glimpses into the life of a nation of both significant and mundane events. This image captured by Roy, documents a protest held in wake of the unexpected Chinese offensive of 1962. The newly independent country, unprepared for a war of this scale suffered heavy losses in both, human and material terms.

artworks.title: Sadar Bazar Fire
artworks.description: This undated image by Kulwant Roy illustrates firemen dousing a fire in Delhi's Sadar Bazar. Roy managed to capture and immortalise many such images, that did not document any significant event but the story told in these photographs is of the building of a nation through the unremitting toil of its citizens, no matter the scale of that toil. The images that we see are rooted in the climate of the times, the beliefs in development through industrial growth and the harnessing of science and technology.

artworks.title: Landscape of Chamba, Himachal Pradesh 1950
artworks.description: In this series of images, Kulwant Roy’s camera dwells not in the moment but goes far beyond to capture an entire ambience. Roy travelled to Kashmir in the 1950s and was quite likely the first photographer to document the Amarnath pilgrimage. He traversed the Himalayas, capturing the beauty of the Chamba landscape and the play of light and shade its peaks rendered.

artworks.title: Roy in New York in the early 1960s
artworks.description: In 1958, Kulwant Roy set off on his world travels, buying a last minute ticket to accompany a friend to England. His travels lasted close to three years and took him to over 30 countries through Europe and North America as well as to the Caribbean, Peru, Colombia and across the Pacific to the Philippines, Japan and Hong Kong. Towards the end of his trip, he mailed a large number of his photographs and negatives back to India but these never arrived. It was a devastating loss, wiping out years of his work.

artworks.title: Photograph of Envelop
artworks.description: This series of photographs by Kulwant Roy were taken just a few days after the Indian army had seized the Haji Pir Pass during the Indo-Pak war in 1965. The tricolour as a symbol of triumph is borne by the Indian troops with the Pir Panjal range as a backdrop; sentinels guarding the hard-won heights. Roy was part of the group of photographers taken to record the victory – and presumably raise national morale.

artworks.title: Stillness of the evening hour
artworks.description: F. R. Ratnagar's pictures are meditative, brimming with a stillness that is not stagnant. The fantastic play of light and shade in his images demonstrate his mastery over chiaroscuro. Ratnagar captured a variety of subjects through his lens, from scenes of village life in India to the canals of Venice to artistic, experimental portraits, his range was not limited by anything. His images of nature encapsulate large vistas of landscapes dotted with a solitary figure or two, bringing out their beauty.

artworks.title: The Solitary sail
artworks.description: The seacape above by Ratnagar has a dream-like quality achieved through manipulated printing and exposure techniques that lend it a slight blur and tonal variations characteristic of pictorialism. There was an equal emphasis on printing techniques, bringing alive photographs to look like paintings. As pictorialist J.N. Unwalla put it, “when photography is used as a medium of depicting and preserving mere incidents it becomes at once mechanical, lifeless and unemotional and is deprived of its place in the fine arts. The aim of the photo-artist is to transmit his own emotions and ideas about his subject to those that view it. Be it a portrait, a figure-study, a landscape or even a still-life picture, it must have the stamp of that artist’s feelings." The landscape above has a dream-like quality achieved through manipulated printing and exposure techniques that lend it a slight blur and tonal variations characteristic of pictorialism.

While the presentation of reality often has dream-like elements in it. His technique involves a fine and a precise style defining the form and the theme in his works. This painting depicts the toil and the labour the workers go through, with the depiction of the lame figure.

artworks.title: The Paik Rebellion of Orissa
artworks.description: The painting is one of the 52 works M.R. Acharekar was commissioned for on the commemorative occasion celebrating the completion of the first hundred years of the freedom movement (1757- 1856). Partha Mitter in his book 'The Triumph of Modernism: India's Artists and the Avant-garde, 1922-47' writes, "Acharekar specialized in a loose impressionist style with heavy impasto colours, quick brush strokes and loose application of paint, to build up a sketch-like rough surface with speckled light distributed over the whole painted surface." Acharekar in this impressionistic style that Partha Mitter speaks of created the 52 set of paintings that are infused with the rebellion and the hostilities of wars organised by the untrained tribal folks and the civilians against the private army of East India Company. The resentment against foreign rule and the atrocities at the hand of the Company had stirred a political turmoil which resulted in uprising in different parts of the country. The patriotic emotions and the struggle of the natives is well encapsulated in the paintings specially executed by the artist.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'M. R. Acharekar' in English in the bottom-right corner of the painting with brush.

artworks.title: Harbour Of Trincomalee
artworks.description: Fritz Eisel was a German painter and graphic artist. His works are highly impressionistic in nature. This landscape from the Harbour Of Trincomalee is a similar impression with the use of the fresh colours and brush strokes.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Khakhar's works are figurative in nature, concerned with the human body and its identity. As a self-proclaimed homosexual, the problem of gender identities became a major theme of his works.

artworks.title: Genesis
artworks.description: De was known for his Neo Tantric style of paintings which was dominated by concentric rings, cresents and orbs. This style was symbolic with meanings. The use of the blue tones bringing in the magical quality to the work symbolises the union of the Purusha and Prakriti, the union of the male and female forms.

artworks.title: R.N.Tagore
artworks.description: Nandalal preferred drawing from life, often sketching outdoors with the subject being life, nature studies, landscapes, figure drawings and animals. He also experimented with printmaking in his long artistic career. In the above print, the artist has depicted Rabindranath Tagore, who reshaped Indian art with contextual modernism in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The illustration is rendered with bold, firm yet fluid strokes gouged into wood and transferred on the plain surface with the help of ink, articulating the contours of the elongated figure.

artworks.title: Meerabai
artworks.description: Nandalal Bose's work reflects changing landscapes, portraits, sketches from life and places at the time of changing outlook in the modern Indian cultural domain. While in the murals he painted at many places like at Shantiniketan and Kirti mandir at Baroda, he reflects taking references from the traditional themes and Indian mythology. His nature to explore the various materials and mediums allowed him to make a prolific body of work in different mediums. Along with his explorations of art learning from the style of the Tagores, he also imbibed the techniques of art from the European indigenous tradition and the Japanese wash technique. This painting reflects a style inspired from the folk paintings and traditional miniature paintings, considering the composition, the women depicted in the works and the details contoured with delicate lines. Such aspects are also reflected in the murals that Nandalal has painted.

artworks.title: A lady with Lotus
artworks.description: Haripura posters by Nandalal capture moments of everyday Indian village life and culture. In this poster, he has depicted a sensuous figure of a woman holding a lotus. The figure is filled with expression of her mood and character, executed with vibrant earthy colours and spontaneous, energetic contouring lines aptly limn the figure with the artist's personal sensibilities toward Indian folk arts.

metadata.inscription: Signed 'Nanda' in Bengali along the right margin of the poster.

artworks.title: Mountains Trees and Houses
artworks.description: This painting belongs to a series of monochromatic ink and watercolour paintings inspired by the Sumi-e Japanese technique the artist employed in the last phase of his life. These compositions were stripped to the bare minimum where only a few strokes of ink were employed to create natural forms in an effortless approach. The above painting belongs to the 'Mountains, trees and Houses' series. The artist has executed mountains, trees and houses, with a range of strokes in tonal variations capturing the rhythm and pattern of the image. This painting was purchased from the collection of Shri Biswaroop Bose and Smt. Nivedita Bose, children of Nandalal.

metadata.inscription: Dated '18.8.59' and signed 'Nanda' in Bengali vertically in the bottom-left corner of the painting with brush in black colour. The painting also bears the artist's personal seal in red.

artworks.description: Hebber was known for his line drawings and the very local and rural themes of his art works. This painting of his shows the masterful strokes of his unique style with the angular and bold lines defining the forms of the figures in action.

artworks.title: Dancers
artworks.description: Telly Kettle was a portrait painter to operate in India to document life. This painting of his portrays the dancers before a temple. It is a very naturalistic depiction of the soft drapes, the ornaments, light and the dramatic rhythm around amongst the audiences watching the dance.

artworks.title: Calcutta
artworks.description: The painting depicts a panoramic picture of old Calcutta with the European designs of the buildings in the landscape of open land of the city. A fine documentation of the scenic terrains in the land of India.

artworks.title: Mosque
artworks.description: Thomas Daniell is one of the prominent names of European artist travelling to India in the 18th century among many Europeans who travelled to this new land in search of wealth and new possibilities. His landscapes are known for their picturesque quality and among the best captures of the exotic land. This painting depicts a landscape with the Mosque.

artworks.title: Despair
artworks.description: The artist tries to portray the theme in a very expressive manner of the portrayal with lines and colour to create the purposeful elongation and distortions in the forms of the figures in despair.

His landscapes are known for their picturesque quality and among the best captures of the exotic land. The painting in watercolour on paper depict the view of Fort St. George at Madras.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: A detailed, delicate rendering with pencil by the artist creates a effect of third dimension on the surface, allowing the eye to travel withing the space Dakoji brings out through the fine dense line work.

artworks.title: From Ages To Ages
artworks.description: Naresh Kapuria is multifaceted with his work as a painter, sculptor, installation artist, designer, producer and curator. He works in mixed media and multiple art forms, and also collaborate with visual and performative art forms. He used a range of materials and found objects to create set designs, interactive performance and exhibitions. His innovative practices in different genres like terracotta, theatrical experiments, paintings, rock gardens and other works are all mutations from his inherited life patterns, than external imitations from outside.

artworks.title: Manika
artworks.description: Lalu Prasad Shaw was influenced by the pre independence Company School of art, the traditional Kalighat Pat painting and the Ajanta cave paintings. Nature and the surroundings with the great Bengali middle class were his sources of inspiration, which are seen reflected in his works. Shaw was widely known for his highly stylised portraits of Bengali women and couples. This portrait of the girl named Manika shows his typical style of painting.

artworks.title: Mrs. Dass Gupta Looks At Santiniketan
Painting - 1
artworks.description: Dasgupta in his paintings painted remnants of the 'Babu culture'. He blended these cultures with his inimitable style to form his unique visual language. His canvasses are crowded with bizarre images, which form an integral part of his art, mirroring the society’s disparities and the injustices and the cruelties that exist within it. The figures appearing in his works, suspended in air or upside down, are indicative. They are used for showing the predicament of a middle class man who does not have a secure foot-hold in our society, who has to make several compromises, face disappointments and let go off his dreams and aspirations.

artworks.title: 750th Anniversary Of''The Secret History Of Mongols" 1240-1990
They Also Serve Who Stand And Wait
Painting
artworks.description: Amitava Banerjee paints in a realistic style with his visuals quite dream like and surreal in the way they are composed and rendered. Lines and tones interest Banerjee in his visual practise and their use is witnessed in most of the renderings of his, be it any medium.

artworks.title: Flying From The Horizon
artworks.description: Early works of Moti Zharotia depict beautiful range of pencil drawings. As an artist he had a love for working in bright colours. In his creative search with varied materials he learned the technique of silk screen printing and explored it to the core. His prints depict the beautiful shades of life nature and spirituality. In this work he depicts a floating figure, as if flying from the heavens with patterned landscape in the foreground.

artworks.title: Prithvi
artworks.description: P. Khemraj was inspired by myriad aesthetic styles, from Indian miniature paintings and erotic temple art to European classicism and modern abstraction. Influenced by the rich Buddhist and Jain cave frescoes at Ajanta and Sittanavasal, Khemraj portrays the profound connection between human beings and nature.

artworks.title: Land - Energy, Architecture
artworks.description: Palaniappan works with a dual perspective in his art with is interest in mathematics, astronomy and as an artist. His minimalist abstract works whether intricately etched prints, spare drawings or avant garde mixed media visual renderings, reflect his fascination with flight, movement and space.

artworks.title: Unusual Relationship
artworks.description: Lines become very important for Shridhar Iyer as an artist. His drawing reflect a keen eye of observing every details like in the details of decorative art practices or the oriental arts. This paintings the morphed form of various creatures like a parrot, reptiles, and other birds like bat, and eagle, show the unusual relationship between the living on this earth. Very colourful and patterned rendering make the painting almost decorative in its look.

artworks.title: Untitled - 1
artworks.description: Works of Seema Ghurayya are abstract renderings with colour and with themes like silence, lightness and freshness. The colour is the medium of expression and feelings in her works.

artworks.title: The Last Days
artworks.description: Various coloured figures indicative of the different natures and kind of people come in the depiction of this work representing the last days of the diseased shown in the painting lying in centre at the foreground, breaks the otherwise vertical layout of visual with the standing figures mourning for the diseased.

artworks.title: Incarnation
artworks.description: Ramachandran's art is marked by references to India's mural traditions, with a strong control over line, vigorous brush work and mastery over colour. In this painting the tribal woman stands in in tribhanga, a sensuous pose with her knees and hips slightly bent, holding a flower in hand. a signature style of Ramachandran, he registers his presence in the painting with his portrait in the Kurmavatar, who carried the statuesque woman on his back.

artworks.title: City Scape
artworks.description: A beautifully complex rendering of the City Scape by the artist, with repeating motifs, line drawing and finely observed detailed panoramic cluster of the elements in the city.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: This Intaglio print on paper depicts a figure with the horse motifs very inspired form the folk and the rural traditional art forms of India. Most of Goud's art was centred on the rural.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Anjolie Ela Menon was inspired by the Early Christian art. One can see its characteristics reflecting in her art too. The frontal perspective in which one can see the figures emerging out, elongated bodies as seen in the murals of the Christian churches which were to be viewed from the ground. The female nude is a frequent subject in her works along with the relationship of the erotic and melancholy, with the thematic depiction of black crows, empty chairs, windows and hidden figures reflecting an iconography of distance and loss.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: The works of Ravi Mandlik are the renderings of the infinite space where natural and organic forms float in harmony. His painting techniques comprise of subtle forms made with delicate raised effects made with colour and textures and the play of light and shade. His art is inspired by landscapes, weathered rock forms, wind and water abrasions, forests and mountains, capturing the relation between various elements and their reaction with living organisms.

artworks.title: Painting - 1
artworks.description: Powerful application of the colour to create the textured canvases of the artist. This painting shows a landscape rendered in the warm colours by the artist. The figures and forms emerge out of the textured surface with the darker rendering of these forms as if bulging out. Here one can see the details of the landscapes emerging out in the similar fashion.

artworks.title: Victory
artworks.description: The painting depicts the victory over the demon Mahisasura. A beautiful interpretation by the artist about the popular theme from the Indian art portraying Mahishasuramardini.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: An abstract landscape with blue, yellow and black colour washes.

artworks.title: Musical Box
artworks.description: Jagdish Chander’s art concerns with the portrayal of pure emotions. For this he uses the Human face to show the myriad expressions portraying anger, angst, bewildernment, happiness, triumph , and such other expressive emotions. His artistic process includes building of the composition slowly layer by layer. His application of colour is in quick strokes pushed hard against the boundaries of control. Visually and psychologically his paintings manifest tension rather that providing the viewer with a restful and a calm feeling.

artworks.title: Lotus
artworks.description: Nandalal's work depicts changing landscapes, portraits of people, sketches from life and places at the time of changing outlook in the modern Indian cultural domain. His nature to explore the various materials and mediums allowed him to make a prolific body of work in different mediums. Bose's sketches captures lived life, people and animals, in the settings with the context and references, with fine rhythmic lines be it pencil, brush, or any medium. Most of his sketches have a strong tendency of documentation and show a continuous involvement with the surroundings that the artist was present in. There are many works that he sketched from his observations of nature in watercolours. This painting is a watercolour rendering of a lotus flower.

artworks.title: Youth
artworks.description: This painting very narrative in format depicts youth with the free strokes of colour and rapid like work. The birds reflect the freedom and fearless flight of the young generation.

artworks.title: Boats
artworks.description: The landscapes is painted with an eye for detail with boats parked on the shore in the foreground and the houses with their embellished motifs painted in the rich colours of lapis lazuli and golden yellow enhancing their beauty in the landscape.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Fine linear lines capture and define the contours of the nude figure. It is a sketch study of the life and human anatomy by the artist Gopal Ghose.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: The essence of the atmosphere, the blowing wind and the chills in the landscape is captured by the artist with the colour wash technique. The artist was successful in integrating the western modernism and sublimity and mysteriousness of the eastern art.

artworks.title: Under Water 1
artworks.description: The essence of the surfing waters, the energy is captured with the a few colours and the effects of the surf rendered by the artist with various media.

artworks.title: Kamet
artworks.description: Many of Pasricha's later works were inspired by the Himalayas and Nicholas Roerich. He worked with watercolours with distinct brushstrokes and use of lines and colour. He climbed the Kamet and Mana peaks to on the spot capture them on his canvases.

artworks.title: Untitled

artworks.title: A Couple Bathing In A Pool Of Water
artworks.description: The painting depicts a landscape with the couple bathing in a pool of water. The tonal shades of blue, green, the darker tones showing the spatial depths and the figures define the artist's style.

artworks.title: A Women Laying On The Ground In Landscape
artworks.description: The painting depicts a landscape with the women lying on the green grass of the landscape. The tonal shades of blue, green and the darker tones showing the spatial depths and the dark tonal voluptuous female body define the paintings of the artist.

artworks.title: Women Seated On A Rock With Her Hands Raised Above

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: His work reflect his concern about the rate at which expanding cities are invading the open spaces and natural landscapes and the environment and his own experiences as a man from a humble town with a simple lifestyle thrown unprepared into the chaos of urban spaces. One can sense, in his works, the pain caused by the displacement of self and physical body, and the struggles of trying to exist in a familiar land and not a refugee.

artworks.title: The Face
artworks.description: The print is a very interesting playful portrayal of the face, with bright colours, geometric and forceful line renderings. The depiction shows both comic and shocking gestures which contradict each other and add a playful element to the visual.

artworks.title: Inner Reflection Of The Human World -x-98
artworks.description: This woodcut print is a very interesting and a detailed depiction of the artists views on subconscious. Surreal as the title is - 'the Inner reflections of the Human world', the visual depicts elongated, serpentine and morphed figures, as signs and symbols appearing in a persons dreams.

artworks.title: Monu Parthar
artworks.description: Nareen Nath's canvases are constructions of the abstract motifs and geometric forms. His canvases have expressive colour effects, weather it be the dense colour tones or subtle fresh shades.

artworks.title: After Image - ||
artworks.description: Jagdish Chander’s art concerns with the portrayal of pure emotions. For this he uses the Human face to show the myriad expressions portraying anger, angst, bewildernment, happiness, triumph , and such other expressive emotions. His artistic process includes building of the composition slowly layer by layer. His application of colour is in quick strokes pushed hard against the boundaries of control. Visually and psychologically his paintings manifest tension rather that providing the viewer with a restful and a calm feeling.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: D L N Reddy is a figurative painter, the figures in whose works are reflecting mood than meaning. His figurative renderings are voluminous, executed with the economic use of visual means. The nude figure, weather squatting, reclining, sitting is a leitmotif in several of his paintings.

artworks.title: Ideas
artworks.description: Anandajit Ray’s works are diverse, including miniaturist works in gouache, cut up paintings rearranged as visual puzzles, and large sculptural installations, animated with a sense of the surreal. In his works on can see a simultaneous exploration of the mundane along with the phantasmal, the ridiculous and the horrific.

artworks.title: If Wishes Were Horses
artworks.description: In his paintings, V. Ramesh recreates dream worlds, comprising landscapes and animals and human beings. Broad brush strokes and thick lines of colour, combined with a grazing technique, characterize his dramatic works.

artworks.title: Techno Landscape - ||
artworks.description: The artist is known for his technical landscapes where in he creates the panoramic construction of the virtual, technical, mechanical construction in form of a natural landscape. With the depictions of the nexus of the material and the virtual connections in his prints the artist tries to portray the urban landscape of technical and digital network.

artworks.title: Aries Vuncent
artworks.description: An artist like Veer Munshi is one of the few painters in India today who is able to transform his experiences as an exiled refugee into the language of painting. His works are the reflection of the socio - political conditions of his land, Kashmir. His works aim to reflect and create awareness. His figures seem to mirror different emotions His canvases present images that are intriguing, beyond the notions of reality and dwell into a surreal realm. In this work he comparatively portrays the artist in him and the artistic struggles of Van Gogh and the weathering sunflowers.

artworks.title: Retake Of Amrita Sher Gil
artworks.description: Re-take of Amrita Sher-Gil is a series of black and white digital photo montages based on archival photographs from the Sher-Gil family. The original photographer was Sundaram's grandfather Umrao Singh. Vivan Sundaram reconfigured the photographs and recast the family in new roles, retelling family history.

artworks.title: Fisher Women
artworks.description: Benod Behari Mukherjee was a key figure in the Contextual Modernism. His style was a complex fusion of idioms absorbed from Western modern art and the spirituality of oriental traditions (both Indian and Far-Eastern). Some of his works show a marked influence of Far-Eastern traditions, namely calligraphy and traditional wash techniques of China and Japan. This work is a simple collage with paper cuts and watercolours, depicting a fisher women.

In his own works describing the forms in his works he says, “.. my forms would function as pure colour in space.” His earlier canvases were characterised by single dominant colour in the background, on which lighter and more complex forms, both geometric and organic. Later his forms were absorbed and symbolised by the colour forms, making the visuals simple in outlook and complex in conception.

artworks.title: Naked Sky Line Porous Air
artworks.description: Kallat has created a distinctive style with his earlier work based on the the common man, the faceless people who remain outside the circle of power in urban India. His works create a dramativ statement and many motifs and symbols are seen to resurface such as the protruding brain. Kallat not only uses the paint and brush but also incorporates other media such as silk screen into his work to give it a more theatrical effect.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: One among the Progressive artists, Souza’s art covered range of subjects from still life, landscapes, nudes and icons of Christianity, rendered boldly with a frantic distortion of form. His works were expressive with his style influenced by the western moderns.

artworks.title: Independence News

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: An abstractionist par excellence, Sheila Makhijani’s abstract works on paper display an intimate and intricate array of lines and colours. In her works one can see a very controlled rendering of the cluster of lines are bathed in very light, almost disappearing, spread of semi-transparent watercolours. With this visual treatment the artist creates the idea of an alternate world to the one we live in.

artworks.title: Drawing - 3
artworks.description: A master of lines, Jogen Chowdhury makes the curves of lines depict the character of the figures in his art. The figures of men and women in his works are caricaturish, wrought by the combination of ‘decorative wilfulness’ and ‘expressive distortion’ and imbued with a sensuality. His drawings in ink on paper are sketchy and quick documentation of of the visuals from mind and surround, different in visual language compared to the decorative and detailed elements of his paintings.

artworks.title: Drawing
artworks.description: Nagji Patel is known for his singular, simple motifs that contain in his sculptures with a subtle erotic grace and his public sculptures, colossal in form with their great social impact. Another facet of his artistic personality is reflected in his drawings in pen and ink, which are his conceptual studies earlier ones in black and white and later ones in colour. For his drawings like in this image, he has a peculiar way of wielding the pen, used in creating small lines and jabs, as if marks made with a chisel.

artworks.title: House Of Ancester
artworks.description: In the art of Sumedh Rajendran, he makes a conscious decision to raise the awareness about the sad state of affairs around him. In his sculptures one can see the amalgamation of various fundamental forms such as animals, objects and humans, resulting in hybrid species that breaks down all preconceived notions one may have while categorising anything into a type. For this he uses industrial materials such as ceramic tiles, steel, iron and other unbending resources by transforming tough, basic materials into a very organic form which shape his installations.

artworks.description: The visual is composed with the subtle hues with bold and prominent brush strokes, depicting an inseparable connect between the urban spaces and the natural areas, marked by the vegetation and the wild life. The spatial depths of the composition are very uniquely rendered by the artist and the colours he has used differentiating the material urban settings from the natural vegetative setting, are very illustrative in nature.

artworks.title: The Red End
artworks.description: Hema Upadhyay works in the varied genres of paintings and sculptural installations, with the use of collage and photographs. Her works derived inspirations from the metropolis of Mumbai highlighting issues such as migrations, dislocation, multicultural aspects of the city, and else. Her works are about stories, real and imaginative. Her works are autobiographical in nature or one can say it is a recurrent theme in her works. Her work is detailed with symbolic motifs and characters woven in the visual depths.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: A abstract rendering with paper pulp and colour on paper by the artist.

artworks.title: Untitled - 8
artworks.description: Jayashree Chakraborty’s works, as she herself mentions, “are like her personal diary of her days in France and the influences.” Her early works reflect influences from the French impressionists and the Byzantine mosaic designs. While her recent work is very close to Nature both in the aspects of subject and material.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: In works of Chintan Upadhyay one can see a meaningful juxtaposition experimented with a series of still lives. In the city of Mumbai he finds a sense of alienation form its inhabitants, which gain a face in his works in form of alien like pictures for which he experiments with caricature, creates satires of the world around him through visual jokes and puns. He doesn’t work in a particular style throughout years. After a series of works his style is varied. But his visual expressions are strong and vibrant. His works come out in layers reflecting the styles that have influenced him : the traditional miniature style that he picked up from around his home town, the abstract styled that he has seen in the works of his father and the narrative style from the Baroda school artists like Gulam Mohammed Sheikh and Bhupen Khakkar.

artworks.description: Sen is known for his caricatures which reflect strong socio-political basis, and his female nude drawings. His style shows an influence of Western Modern art and the traces of cubism. His works thus reflect the two dimensional, structured planes but still creates an illusion of voluptuousness. His drawings and paintings can be defined by the strong lines and bold and stylised strokes. Colour plays an important role in his work, but the expressive life sketches are the dominant part in his art. His works mainly captures the everyday urban life rendered from a cynical and detached perspective, a typical sen’s viewpoint.

artworks.title: Dog In The Bush Exclusive
artworks.description: Komu works in different media and genres. His work carries a symbol of protest in them and refer to the paradoxes of the urban situations, where there are contrasts like glamour, on one hand and poverty, on the other. His works reflect both compassion and cynicism, hope and dejection giving a tribute to the spirit of all those who continue to survive the city and its paradoxes.

His work is multifaceted and complex, exploring the connection between psychological states of mind and socion political behaviours, when seen from the perspective of the individual’s relationship to his external environment.

artworks.title: Old Pebbals New Myths
artworks.description: Rekha Rodwittiya’s works deal with complex issues of life and living, of agreements and dissgreements, of alienation and belonging, of discrimination and acceptance, and so on. As a process of her work she considers it important for her to react pragmatically to socio- political attitudes that surround her. Her work reflect the sensitivity towards socio- political attitudes along with the reflections from her past. Her images are the byproduct of her thoughts and emotions, her readings, observations, beliefs, values and complex experiences of past. Her portrayals of women are looked through the prism of personal experiences and are the reflections from the day to day realities.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Kaleka’s work is based on the themes of animals, sexuality and tradition. His initial work are in a painted format. But his interest in film narratives and cinema lead the advent of video as amedium in his art. His works look surrealist in nature, when the treatment of scenes from everyday life on his canvases is noted. The treatment of forms though quite subtle, his works have a strong symbolic message in them.

artworks.title: Flower Pots
artworks.description: This painting by the artist shows a study of detailed and delicately painted flowers in a pot.

artworks.title: Nights Watch
artworks.description: Reena Saini Kallat's works are conceptual, created with the mediums like drawing, photography, sculpture and video art in diverse materials as official records and registered name lists of people, objects, and monuments that are lost or disappeared without any trace, electrical wires to show barriers and salt to show the weak yet intrinsic relation between body and oceans. She is fascinated with the role that memory plays in not just how we choose to remember but even how we recollect the past. She uses the motif of the rubber stamp as object and imprint signifying the bureaucratic apparatus.

His visuals uniquely portray the different traits and the flaws of the human behaviour, in the faces, body and gestures as devices of irony.
