artworks.title: The Grey World
artworks.description: When the visual language is considered, Samir Aich is a tireless experimenter. In his works he attempts to figurate the abstract concepts like the primordial force of nature, the animal spirit and so on. His works depict these concepts in the form of range of awe inspiring imagery. As far as the technique is considered, the canvas is first painted uniformly and then light is introduced to teh surface by the application of the regular patches of white, green, and tones of red ochre, and then wiping out to bring the play of light and shade. After these layers of transparent washes the figurative element comes. His objects are generally positioned around the nudes, marking the points where their form reflects, intersect and overlap. There is a fluidity and enigma in these visuals that Aich created.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: A symbolic work, created with the medium of oil on canvas. The rendering of space in the painting is surreal in nature, with the symbols of tension and clashes floating in it, contrasting to the lights of hope lit on the realistically rendered ground.

artworks.title: Guarded Joy Of Expection
artworks.description: Jaya Ganguly works with broad and sure brush strokes done in a range of organic rich colours. The figures in her work look massive, primitive and voluminous, and this quality in her work give them a distinct character. The figures in her work are known to have ‘a structural compositional values with a sense of tension and force.’ Men and women both, from orthodox as well as bourgeoisie backgrounds, the ones who survive a monotonous and placid existence , all are the part of her visuals.

artworks.title: Ring - 2
artworks.description: Anju Dodiya's works are largely figurative with the reflection of self as a theme. Her works are highly introspective and personal. Her early work shows a extreme abstraction where she tried to focus her gaze on railway stations, roadside scenes and so forth, but her impulse of the painterly introspection was strong to drive her vision back to represent the situations form her life. This work in particular shows her connection and involvement to the subject.

artworks.title: I Have Heard People Say Things Exist Life Bubbles Do
artworks.description: With the multiple layers found in his style of story telling, one cannot deny the his inspiration from mass media and newspaper clippings. This work also is one telling about the realities or the 'unseen realities' of life in his signature style.

artworks.title: Cities
artworks.description: Born in 1937, Zarina Hashmi is an Indian Born American Artist. She works in three major genres of drawings, printmaking and sculpture. Her works are abstract and minimal, exploring the concept of home, distance, trajectories influenced by her own extensive travels for which she uses the visual elements from Islamic religious decoration. In her minimalist works she uses the locations which surrounds her, the ones she travelled, to construct new geographies, filling them with fresh perspective and new, universal meaning. She worked on series of woodcut prints titled 'Cities.'

artworks.title: Unit One
artworks.description: Jeram Patel was one of the pioneers of abstract art in India, who turned around the Indian art scene with his powerful visual language and method of abstraction. He used to not create a form, but used the method of destruction to formulate his visuals.His method of abstraction involved engraving on burnt wood that he set alight with blowtorch. This method of his became his style, along with the strokes made with black strokes and shapes of ink on paper.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Jeram Patel was one of the artists who turned around the Indian art scene and formulated a new visual identity and method of abstraction in the late 1950's and 60's. Alongside N.S. Bendre and Sankho Chowdhuri who set up the Baroda School of Art. His works essentially monochromatic in nature are comprised of his iconic black strokes which reveal the artist’s fascination with the hidden and the interior, many a times not a very pleasant place. He also devices a destructive method for creating his visuals, like the ones made with the blowtorch. Similarly the space of interior in his work depict the theatre of violence. The patterns in his works are intricate and the black form have a effect of movement in the bold but supple strokes used by him.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Benod Behari Mukherjee was a key figure in the Contextual Modernism. His style was a complex fusion of idioms absorbed from Western modern art and the spirituality of oriental traditions (both Indian and Far-Eastern). Some of his works show a marked influence of Far-Eastern traditions, namely calligraphy and traditional wash techniques of China and Japan.

artworks.title: Untitled
artworks.description: Kartick Pyne was an artist much ahead of his contemporaries. When the major stress was on painting in Real, Kartick broke through the convention and started incorporating the irrational elements and portrayals beyond the real. His works incorporated complicated metaphors and what critics called 'free form Images'. This painting with watercolours on paper depicts a donkey taking the load on his back.

artworks.title: Anyam
artworks.description: Elizabeth Brunner was a Hungarian artist born in 1910. Her mother Elizabeth Sass Brunner too was an artist who had exhibited in the National Salon from 1914. Both the mother and daughter artist- duo lived and travelled in India extensively and went on many pilgrimage tours in and around the country with an artistic interest. Brunner along with her mother Elizabeth Sass came to India in the year 1930 in search of new path in life and became respected figures in Indian artistic life with their subjects of work concentric on the life and spirit of India. In India they were received by Ravindranath Tagore in Shantiniketan and by several Maharajas and other prominent Indian spokesmen in other parts of country. In the time they spend in India they also painted many paintings with Buddhist themes. Apart from this, throughout their travel together; they painted landscapes, mountains, forests, monuments and people along with major Indian personalities.

artworks.title: Mahatma's Silent Day

The painting is done in the medium of oil on a palm leaf mat and brilliantly gives the essence of the Pindaya cave which is an important pilgrimage site for Buddhist in Burma and an attractively unusual visual sight for tourists with thousands of Buddha images in various styles

artworks.title: Let Sleeping Dogs Lie Series, Bombay
artworks.description: ‘Mumbai as a home binding millions of people together’becomes a theme for this photographer which she captures in a series of photographs titled ‘Home in the City’. In this series of monochromatic photographs she captures well known personalities who lived or visited Mumbai, as well as strangers she happened to meet. This photograph is from the series 'let sleeping dogs lie'.

artworks.title: Black Gold
artworks.description: A panoramic landscape with the buffalo herders. The painting comes as a bright visual with the contrast of the yellow background to the black buffaloes to the viewer. It is a beautifully composed work with the village huts and trees in the multiple perspective through the length of the landscape.

artworks.title: Miserable Attelage
artworks.description: A black and white photograph capturing the atmosphere, light and the tones of the landscape with the team trapped in the stormy climate in the rains. It is a quick and a clear capture of the thematic depths of the landscape.

artworks.title: Cattle Tracks
artworks.description: A beautiful black and white photograph capturing the panoramic depths of a village landscape showing the cattle tracks.

artworks.title: Promise Of Rain
artworks.description: A photograph capturing dark clouds over the landscape of a village, promising it rain.

artworks.title: Portrait Of A House
artworks.description: Bendre is known as a supreme landscapist, a composer and master of colours. He was influenced by the tradition of miniature paintings. After a tour to the western nations he imbibed the western influence in his art and created a niche for himself in the field of art with a style of his own. His paintings depict subtle themes ranging from everyday life, surrounding, architecture to the abstract themes. This work depicts the portrait of houses.

artworks.title: Near Walberswick
artworks.description: This watercolour rendering shows a landscape near Walberswick.

artworks.title: Shimmering Froms
artworks.description: Dakoji Devraj’s canvases and prints are full of animals and strokes. Most of his prints are in black and white, but some like this one in the image have hue of the colours and playful atmosphere. His imagery is charged with energy and mystery.

artworks.title: Painting
artworks.description: Landscapes in Paramjit Singh's works are surreal. They encompassed deep pictorial spaces and shadows cast by the inanimate objects, located or floating in the space are very modelled and plastic in nature.

artworks.title: Life Movement
artworks.description: Reddy's prints, often done in semi-abstract or abstract forms, revolve around subjects from nature, besides human figures. He was the pioneer of the colour viscosity process, in which a metal plate is etched with acid or prepared with machine driven tools to form several layers. Intaglio colour is applied by hand and excess ink, especially from the upper layers, is wiped off. The remaining colours are prepared with linseed oil. Each colour has a different viscosity so as to repel each other on the plate. These colours are then rolled on the plate, with the help of rollers of different degrees of softness, the hardest reaching the lowest layers. Each print appears as an individual multicoloured image.

artworks.title: Ajenta
artworks.description: A lithograph by this French artist with his typical portrayal of the human form and the collage format from a Gujarati newsletter reflects a Indian inspiration in the print.
